* **Active** — The vault is open for deposits and the leader can trade normally.
* **Paused** — The leader (or an admin) has paused the vault. No new deposits are accepted, but the leader can still trade to close positions. Withdrawal requests can still be submitted, and pending withdrawals continue to be processed.

### Public Vault Data

The following vault information is publicly visible to all users:

* Vault name, description, and type
* Leader identity and commission rate
* Total value, share price, and number of depositors
* Historical deposits and withdrawals
* Portfolio metrics (PnL, TVL, APR)
* All open positions and trade history (via the vault's account ID)

This transparency allows depositors to evaluate vault performance before committing capital.


# SLP Vault

The Strike LP Vault is the protocol-managed vault that provides market liquidity and serves as the Strike Liquidity Provider (SLP). Depositors receive shares in a common pool of capital used for market making, liquidation backstop positions, and authorized Credit Recovery.

The market-making system was developed in collaboration with a professional market-making firm and is managed by the Strike team. The vault also assumes the protocol's former Insurance Fund responsibilities: receiving adaptive liquidation fees, accepting eligible backstop positions, acquiring recovered Credit collateral, and absorbing recognized terminal Credit losses.

All of these activities affect the same vault and its ordinary shares. LP returns depend on their combined gains and losses; they are not a fixed interest payment or a guaranteed spread return.

### How the vault provides liquidity

The market-making system places bid and ask quotes across supported markets. It distributes liquidity along a curve, concentrating more depth near its reference price and less depth at wider price levels. This provides executable liquidity while allowing spreads, depth, and inventory exposure to be adjusted by market.

Quotes use an external reference built from major exchange prices rather than relying solely on Strike's own order book. The system also evaluates stale or mispriced resting orders against that reference and can trade against them when an opportunity exists.

Each fill changes the vault's exposure. Spread capture contributes to returns, while commissions, rebates, funding, and the cost of carrying and reducing inventory determine the net result. Adverse price movement or one-sided order flow can outweigh the spread earned.

#### Inventory and volatility controls

The system adjusts its quoting according to exposure, volatility, and margin usage. When the vault is long, more competitive asks encourage other traders to buy from it, reducing its long exposure, while less competitive bids discourage further accumulation. When it is short, the adjustment works in the opposite direction.

During higher volatility or margin usage, the system can widen spreads, reduce quoting depth, and restrict new exposure. Per-market position controls influence how aggressively it quotes on the side that would increase inventory. Parameters are managed per market; their exact values are operational settings rather than fixed protocol guarantees.

These controls govern market-making activity. SLP Backstop transfers use separate engine admission checks and are not subject to the retired Insurance Fund utilization or notional caps.

### What contributes to LP returns

| Activity                  | Effect on the vault                                                                          |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Market making             | Realized trading PnL and unrealized gains or losses on positions that remain open            |
| Stale-order trading       | Gains or losses from executions against prices that differ from the external reference       |
| Funding                   | Receipts or payments according to position direction and the funding rate                    |
| Adaptive liquidation fees | Income from eligible solvent liquidation fills, subject to the market's fee and surplus caps |
| Backstop positions        | Gains or losses from receiving, netting, carrying, and reducing inherited exposure           |
| Credit collateral sales   | Realized gains or losses relative to the collateral's recorded acquisition cost              |
| Terminal Credit losses    | A balance debit for borrower debt remaining after authorized recovery is exhausted           |
| Later Bad Debt repayment  | A balance credit when previously recognized borrower debt is collected                       |

Normal trading commission does not become SLP income merely because the SLP is the backstop. Adaptive liquidation fees are a separate charge credited to the vault. Direct backstop and ADL fills are fee-free; they still change exposure and can realize PnL.

For a perpetual position with signed quantity **Q**, Mark Price **P**, and funding rate **f**, the funding cashflow is:

$$
\text{Funding payment}=-QPf
$$

Positive **Q** means long and negative **Q** means short. A positive funding rate makes longs pay and shorts receive; a negative rate reverses that direction.

### Shares and vault value

Let **B** be the vault's recorded USD balance. For position **i**, let **Qᵢ** be signed size, **eᵢ** entry price, and **Pᵢ** current Mark Price. Total perpetual unrealized PnL is:

$$
T=\sum\_i(P\_i-e\_i)Q\_i
$$

The sum includes both Cross and Isolated positions. Vault net asset value is:

$$
\mathrm{NAV}=B+T
$$

Isolated collateral is already part of **B** and is not added again. For positive NAV and outstanding share count **S**:

$$
\text{Share price}=\frac{\mathrm{NAV}}{S}
$$

$$
\text{Holding value}=\text{shares held}\times\text{Share price}
$$

A deposit of **D** receives shares at the settlement share price, rounded down to the supported share precision:

$$
\text{New shares}=\operatorname{floor}\_{8\text{ decimals}}
\left(\frac{D}{\text{Share price}}\right)
$$

With no outstanding shares, the initial share price is USD 1. The SLP uses ordinary vault issuance and redemption rules, including the zero-share-price deposit reset. In that reset, stale shares are cleared before new deposit shares are issued. It does not automatically restore losses or inject capital.

There is one ordinary share class, with no protected SLP seed holder or special minimum share floor. The active SLP account cannot hold shares in its own vault or own Credit Lines. Other accounts may borrow against eligible SLP shares under the Credit rules.

### Liquidation backstop exposure

When an ordinary trader's liquidation reaches backstop handling, Strike selects a settlement price and simulates the entire receiving fill against the SLP portfolio. An incoming long can reduce an existing SLP short, close it, or reverse it into a long. An incoming short behaves symmetrically.

Acceptance requires nonnegative projected Available Balance and acceptable health across every open Cross and Isolated margin profile. For profiles with positive Maintenance Margin, projected equity must be positive and the margin ratio must remain strictly below 90%. Orders, unrealized PnL, tier changes, and Isolated collateral movements are included.

If the SLP rejects the position, ordinary ADL uses the same selected Backstop Price. Accepting a position does not guarantee a profitable exit, and the transfer itself generates no fee income.

See SLP Backstop for price selection, netting equations, admission boundaries, and fallback ADL.

### Credit collateral inventory

Authorized Credit Recovery can transfer borrower collateral into SLP custody. The vault owns that collateral and records its acquisition cost by asset. Current custody is the sole inventory quantity source.

Inventory is valued at acquisition cost rather than continuously marked to market. Let **Fₐ** be the remaining cost of asset **a**:

$$
F=\sum\_a F\_a,\qquad U=B-F
$$

Here **F** is the Conversion Reserve and **U** is Unreserved USD. The accounting identity is:

$$
\mathrm{NAV}=U+F+T=B+T
$$

The reserve explains why recorded balance and NAV can exceed immediately spendable USD. Inventory is not added to NAV a second time. Changes in its market value become realized gains or losses when it is sold.

#### Acquiring collateral

Credit Recovery determines which collateral can be taken and in what quantity. Healthy collateral is not sold just to replenish SLP cash. Where recovery also redeems vault shares, that leg settles first and collateral acquisition is recomputed from the resulting state.

For accepted collateral quantity **q**, reference price **P₀**, and conversion discount **c**:

$$
K=qP\_0(1-c)
$$

The borrower transfers the collateral. Debt reduction **d** equals the outstanding debt if **K** covers it; otherwise **d** is **K** truncated downward to eight decimal places. Any difference **K − d** is credited to the borrower as USD surplus, and the Credit Facility releases exposure **d**.

The SLP records the full **K** as acquisition cost:

$$
B'=B,\qquad F'=F+K,\qquad U'=U-K
$$

Acquisition does not debit the SLP's recorded balance. It moves value from Unreserved USD into inventory carried at cost, leaving NAV unchanged. Authorized acquisition can make **U** negative and leave existing payout claims temporarily unfunded.

#### Selling inventory

An independent buyer pays from its own spendable USD to purchase an exact quantity of SLP-owned collateral. At accepted reference price **P₁** and collateral sale discount **s**:

$$
\text{Quoted payment}=qP\_1(1-s)
$$

The configured sale discount satisfies **0 ≤ s ≤ c**. A purchase requires valid pricing, sufficient inventory, representable asset units, and sufficient buyer funds within the buyer's payment cap. It either settles in full or is rejected. The buyer receives custody; the sale does not further reduce the original borrower's debt.

Let **V** be the actual posted payment and **k** the inventory cost released. A partial sale releases proportional cost; a full sale releases the asset's entire remaining cost. Before decimal-rounding effects:

$$
\Pi\_{\mathrm{inventory}}=V-k
$$

$$
B'=B+(V-k),\qquad F'=F-k,\qquad U'=U+V
$$

Only the gain or loss increases or decreases recorded balance. Releasing reserved cost explains why Unreserved USD increases by the full funded payment. Settlement uses actual represented payment and cost changes and recomputes the total reserve.

Because shares use inventory acquisition cost, a new depositor can participate in an inventory gain that arose before entry. An exiting holder can leave an unrealized inventory loss to remaining holders. There is no separate share class or historical-holder allocation for these outcomes.

### Terminal Credit losses

Once authorized recovery is confirmed exhausted, the SLP absorbs the full residual debt **Dᵣ**:

$$
B'=B-D\_r
$$

The Credit Facility releases that exposure once, while the borrower's debt remains collectible. Later repayment **p** reduces the retained debt and credits the SLP:

$$
D\_r'=D\_r-p,\qquad B'=B+p
$$

Repayment does not release Facility exposure a second time. These losses and recoveries affect the shareholders who hold shares when they are recognized. Loss recognition is not capped by available payout cash and can make balance, Unreserved USD, or NAV negative.

This Credit loss mechanism does not automatically clear negative trader balances left by perpetual liquidation or ADL.

### Fees and withdrawals

As a protocol vault, the SLP has a zero leader performance fee. Trading commissions, funding, and realized losses still affect vault performance.

A withdrawal request reserves shares and starts the configured withdrawal waiting period. The final redemption value uses the share price at execution, so an estimate at request time is not a fixed payout. Shares pledged to Credit also follow the applicable debt-repayment and release rules.

Execution depends on both margin capacity and Unreserved USD. Let **W\_d** be ordinary Withdrawable Balance calculated from full recorded balance, and **C** applicable commitments and reward locks not already deducted by **W\_d**:

$$
\text{Payout limit}=\max\bigl(0,\min(U,W\_d)-C\bigr)
$$

Each commitment is counted once. A positive share value does not guarantee an immediate payout. A request can remain pending while liquidity is insufficient, including when value is held in collateral inventory. Ordinary withdrawal processing can cancel orders or reduce perpetual positions to release capacity, but that does not itself convert collateral inventory into USD.

The payout limit applies to discretionary funded transfers, withdrawals, and redemptions. It does not cap mandatory PnL, fees, funding, backstop settlements, or recognized Credit losses.

#### Example: value and payout capacity

Assume recorded balance of USD 100,000, no perpetual positions, 100,000 shares, and no other commitments. The vault acquires collateral at a cost of USD 30,000, then later sells all of it for USD 27,000.

| Quantity               | Before acquisition | After acquisition | After sale |
| ---------------------- | -----------------: | ----------------: | ---------: |
| Recorded balance       |            100,000 |           100,000 |     97,000 |
| Inventory cost reserve |                  0 |            30,000 |          0 |
| Unreserved USD         |            100,000 |            70,000 |     97,000 |
| NAV                    |            100,000 |           100,000 |     97,000 |
| Share price            |               1.00 |              1.00 |       0.97 |
| Payout limit           |            100,000 |            70,000 |     97,000 |

Acquisition leaves NAV unchanged but reduces payout capacity. The sale realizes a USD 3,000 loss while increasing liquid payout capacity. Until that sale, the inventory's market loss is not reflected in the acquisition-cost share price.

### Margin risk and automatic ADL

The SLP uses ordinary Cross and Isolated margin. Cross positions share a pool; each Isolated position has its own profile. Let **E** be a profile's equity and **H** its Maintenance Margin. For **E > 0**, its margin ratio is **R = H / E**.

| State       | Margin ratio for a positive-equity profile |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Healthy     | Below 70%                                  |
| Margin Call | At least 70%, below 90%                    |
| Reduce Only | At least 90%, below 100%                   |
| Liquidate   | At least 100%                              |

A profile with positive Maintenance Margin and nonpositive equity is bankrupt. Ordinary classification treats zero Maintenance Margin as healthy. Inventory and its cost reserve do not enter these margin formulas; cash shortage alone does not establish margin bankruptcy.

At liquidation or bankruptcy, the SLP enters automatic ADL for the affected profile. Risk-increasing orders are canceled and new perpetual risk is blocked while any episode remains active. Cross recovery reduces Cross positions; an Isolated episode reduces only its own position. The SLP bypasses the ordinary liquidation IOC ladder and cannot backstop itself.

ADL settles at current mark when profile equity is positive or zero, and at raw Bankruptcy Price when equity is negative. Both sides pay zero fees. An active episode ends only when the profile is flat, or when:

$$
E>0\quad\text{and}\quad H\le0.80E
$$

The 80% recovery target differs from the 90% admission boundary and the 100% liquidation trigger. Recovery depends on eligible opposing profitable positions. Insufficient counterparties or an unavailable price leave exposure open and restricted; unfinished recovery survives restart.

Manual ADL is separate: it requests a specified reduction at mark and requires enough opposing capacity for the entire request. It does not use automatic sizing to the 80% target.

### Risks borne by LPs

| Risk                             | Control                                                           | Remaining exposure                                                                      |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Directional and one-sided flow   | Inventory-sensitive quoting and position reduction                | Inventory can grow faster than it can be reduced; losses can be permanent               |
| Volatility and adverse selection | Spread and depth adjustments                                      | Fast price changes can make fills adverse before quotes adapt                           |
| Market concentration             | Per-market quoting controls and margin admission                  | Accepted positions retain market risk until reduced or closed                           |
| Backstop positions               | Full projected margin checks and fallback ADL                     | An accepted transfer can lose value or contribute to SLP distress                       |
| Collateral inventory             | Authorized acquisition, purchase validation, and a payout reserve | Inventory may sell below cost or remain illiquid; NAV can differ from liquidation value |
| Terminal Credit losses           | Recovery before loss recognition and continued debt collection    | The SLP absorbs residual losses, and later collection is uncertain                      |
| Margin distress                  | Reduce-only restrictions and automatic ADL                        | Counterparty shortages and adverse settlement can leave residual exposure or deficits   |
| Withdrawals                      | Waiting periods and funded payout limits                          | Payment can be delayed even while the displayed holding value is positive               |

Depositors participate in all of these risks through the same share price. Market-making controls, backstop admission, and ADL reduce or manage exposure; none guarantees preservation of deposited capital.


# Strike LP Vault Liquidity Program

**Strike covers SLP Vault losses for a full year — July 4, 2026 to July 4, 2027.**

Today we're excited to announce the Strike Liquidity Program, where Strike will cover any potential losses incurred by capital deposited into the Strike Liquidity Provider (SLP) Vault. We expect the vault to make good money — it's already earning around a 20% APR — but this initiative protects against downside risk.

Over the past year, Strike has grown into one of the most active trading venues in the Cardano ecosystem. As volume and participation have increased, one thing has become clear: deep, reliable liquidity is the foundation that makes everything else possible.

Every trade, every position, and every market on Strike depends on liquidity. Without it, there is no efficient execution, no tight spreads, and no scalable growth. The next phase of Strike is about strengthening that foundation and opening it up to users in a meaningful way.

Today, we are introducing a new opportunity to participate directly in powering Strike markets.

By depositing into the Strike LP Vault, users provide the liquidity that trades rely on across all active pairs. Protection applies to all depositors to the vault, regardless of which asset they deposit. This capital is not idle. It is actively deployed through a market making system designed to continuously quote and manage positions across the platform. The same core principles used by professional market makers in global financial markets are applied here, allowing the system to operate efficiently while generating yield from trading activity.

What makes this particularly compelling is a protection mechanism designed to remove the primary barrier to participation.

Strike will cover any losses incurred by capital deposited into the LP Vault — for a full year, up to $2M USD total in the vault. Any covered losses are repaid directly from the Strike treasury.

This means users can participate in powering the market without taking on downside risk. Capital is actively deployed, earns yield from trading activity, and is protected against losses for the duration of the program.

### Strike Liquidity Provider Vault

Most users interact with markets as traders, taking positions and reacting to price movements. The LP Vault offers a different role. Instead of trading within the market, users can power the market itself. Every trade executed on Strike is supported by this liquidity.

The system behind the vault has been built with a focus on performance and reliability, drawing from market making strategies designed to operate in high-volume environments. Rather than passive lending, this is active participation in the core engine that drives trading.

As Strike continues to expand across assets and ecosystems, the importance of scalable liquidity will only increase. The LP Vault is the first step in opening that layer to users in a way that is both accessible and aligned with long-term growth.

### Program Terms

Any losses covered under this program are paid off from the Strike treasury.

* **1 year of coverage.** Runs July 4, 2026 to July 4, 2027.
* **Up to $2M USD total in the vault.** Coverage applies across the vault up to a combined cap of $2M USD in deposited capital.
* **3 months minimum in the vault.** Capital must remain deposited for at least 3 consecutive months to qualify for loss coverage. Coverage runs 3 months from each deposit, so late deposits stay covered even if that period extends past July 4, 2027.
* **Depositing late?** Coverage always runs a full 3 months from your deposit date. For example, a deposit in month 9 (around April 2027) is covered for 3 months from that date — extending past the program's July 4, 2027 end — subject to the $2M vault cap.
* **Already in the vault before July 4, 2026?** You're still covered — under your original terms. See Already in the Vault? below.
* **All depositors are covered.** Protection applies to every depositor to the vault, regardless of which asset they deposit.
* **Only capital deposited at the time is covered.** Coverage applies to the capital deposited at the time of enrollment — it does not automatically extend to amounts added later.
* **Paid from the Strike treasury.** Any covered losses are made directly from the Strike treasury.

### Already in the Vault?

If you deposited into the SLP Vault **before July 4, 2026**, you are already enrolled and remain covered. Nothing changes for you, and no action is required.

* **Your clock started when you deposited — not today.** The time your capital has already spent in the vault counts. Nothing resets to the relaunch date, and no re-deposit is needed.
* **You qualify at 1 month, not 3.** Existing depositors keep the original **1-month minimum hold** to qualify for coverage. The new **3-month minimum** applies only to deposits made from July 4, 2026 onward.
* **Coverage runs 3 months from your deposit — same as it always did.** The loss-coverage duration is unchanged; it simply runs from your original deposit date. Existing capital is automatically included, subject to the $2M vault cap.

In short: pre-existing liquidity providers are grandfathered in. Your time in the vault carries over from your original deposit, you qualify at the easier 1-month threshold, and your prior deposit is honored exactly as it was.

### Quick Guide

1. **Fund your account.** There are a few places to deposit. When prompted, supply either ADA or USDM.
2. **Deposit into the SLP Vault.** After funding your account, go to the vault section and deposit your funds into the Strike Liquidity Provider (SLP) vault.
3. **Hold for at least 3 months.** All liquidity providers who supply for at least 3 consecutive months are eligible. You can withdraw at any time after the 3 months; potential payouts occur after the program completes. *(Already deposited before July 4, 2026? Your original 1-month minimum still applies — see above.)*


# Borrow and Earn

Strike’s credit line lets you keep a supported asset as collateral and use USD-denominated credit to enter **Strike Liquidity Provider (SLP), the only vault currently eligible for credit draws**. SLP is Strike’s official market-making vault. ADA is supported alongside SundaeSwap USDCx/USDM LP tokens and Aave V3 Ethereum aUSDC. **SLP’s vault fee is 0%.**

You retain exposure to your collateral’s price while also taking on the performance of the vault. Your debt is denominated in USD. If the line becomes unhealthy, Strike can redeem the vault shares assigned to it, convert its collateral, or use both to reduce that debt.

Borrowed credit goes directly into SLP and buys SLP shares. You cannot withdraw the draw as cash, transfer it, or use it directly as personal trading margin or bot funding. SLP itself operates under its normal trading rules. References to “the vault” below mean SLP.

The numerical terms below describe the current launch configuration. Settings and vault availability can change. Prices and example returns are illustrative, and the amounts available to draw or release are checked again when an action executes.

### Depositing ADA

Choose the **collateral deposit** route when you want to retain ADA for a credit line. A collateral deposit credits your ADA custody balance without selling the ADA or increasing your spendable USD balance.

The **balance deposit** route is separate: ADA deposited through that route is valued or exchanged for a USD balance. It does not also create ADA collateral. ADA support alone does not make every ADA deposit a collateral deposit.

Follow the deposit instructions and confirmation requirements for the selected route. Sending a transaction and completing its settlement are separate steps; a deposit can appear as pending settlement while Cardano processing completes.

ADA is measured to six decimal places:

$$
1\text{ ADA}=1{,}000{,}000\text{ lovelace}
$$

$$
\text{ADA amount}=\frac{\text{lovelace amount}}{1{,}000{,}000}
$$

For example, an accepted collateral deposit of 1,000,000,000 lovelace credits **1,000 ADA**. A displayed USD valuation of that ADA is a valuation of the asset, not additional spendable dollars.

Depositing ADA does not create debt or automatically pledge it. Opening a line combines a collateral allocation with a draw into SLP. You can also add collateral to an existing line.

### The terms you will see

| Term                          | Meaning                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Custody balance**           | The quantity of a supported asset held for your account within Strike.                                            |
| **Available custody**         | The part of that balance not allocated to any credit line.                                                        |
| **Collateral pledge**         | Allocating available custody to a particular line. The units remain in custody but are locked against withdrawal. |
| **Credit line**               | One account’s debt relationship for one collateral asset and SLP.                                                 |
| **Draw**                      | An increase in USD debt that buys shares directly in that line’s vault.                                           |
| **Debt**                      | The line’s unpaid USD obligation. A fall in ADA’s price does not reduce the dollars owed.                         |
| **Encumbered vault shares**   | Shares assigned to a credit line. Their proceeds are available for repayment and recovery.                        |
| **Unencumbered vault shares** | Shares that are not assigned to a credit line and follow ordinary vault withdrawal rules.                         |
| **Collateral release**        | Moving allocated collateral back to available custody. This is separate from an on-chain withdrawal.              |
| **Recovery**                  | Automatic action to reduce debt when the line crosses a risk boundary.                                            |
| **Debt remainder**            | A specifically confirmed, temporary state with debt left after the last encumbered shares are redeemed.           |
| **Bad debt**                  | Debt remaining after the applicable recovery and backstop process. It remains owed.                               |

**LP** means liquidity provider. The SundaeSwap LP tokens used as collateral represent an interest in the USDCx/USDM liquidity pool. **SLP shares** represent your interest in Strike’s vault. The collateral tokens and the shares purchased with credit have separate valuations and roles.

A line is identified by **account + collateral asset + vault**. With SLP as the only eligible vault, your ADA-backed SLP line and LP-backed SLP line remain separate. Each has its own collateral allocation and debt.

Collateral assigned to one line does not automatically secure another line. Available custody does not automatically top up a line. Shares in the same vault still experience that vault’s common investment performance.

For each asset:

$$
\text{Available custody}=\text{Total custody}-\sum\text{Collateral allocated to its lines}
$$

Suppose you deposit 1,000 ADA and allocate 800 ADA to a line. Your total custody is still 1,000 ADA, but only **200 ADA** is available to withdraw or allocate elsewhere. If 100 pledged ADA is later converted during recovery, both your total custody and the line’s collateral fall by 100 ADA.

### Opening an ADA credit line: a complete example

Assume ADA is valued at $0.50 and SLP’s share price is $1.00.

1. You deposit **1,000 ADA** through the collateral route.
2. You allocate **800 ADA** to the line.
3. The collateral value is **800 × $0.50 = $400**.
4. You draw **$400** into the vault, assuming all admission, minimum deposit, and capacity checks pass.
5. At $1.00 per share, the draw buys **400 encumbered shares**.

Your balances immediately after this example are:

| Item                                 |     Amount |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------: |
| Total ADA custody                    |  1,000 ADA |
| ADA allocated to the line            |    800 ADA |
| Available ADA custody                |    200 ADA |
| USD debt                             |       $400 |
| Encumbered vault shares              | 400 shares |
| Initial value of those shares        |       $400 |
| Spendable USD received from the draw |         $0 |

The ADA stays exposed to ADA’s market price. The shares gain or lose value with the vault. Neither movement automatically changes the USD debt; debt falls when repayment actually settles.

### How much can you draw?

Use these quantities for one line:

| Symbol        | Meaning                                                                                                     |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **q**         | Units of collateral allocated to the line.                                                                  |
| **P**         | Accepted USD price per collateral unit.                                                                     |
| **C = q × P** | The line’s collateral value in USD.                                                                         |
| **s**         | Its encumbered vault shares.                                                                                |
| **S**         | Current USD price per vault share.                                                                          |
| **V = s × S** | The value of those encumbered shares.                                                                       |
| **D**         | Outstanding USD debt.                                                                                       |
| **M**         | Admission ratio: the maximum debt relative to collateral value after a draw or ordinary collateral release. |

The collateral-based borrowing limit is:

$$
D\_{\text{after}}\le M\times C\_{\text{after}}
$$

The current launch admission ratio is **M = 1.00** for all three supported assets. At that ratio, $400 of collateral can support at most $400 of debt at admission, subject to the other checks below.

For an additional draw **B**:

$$
D\_{\text{after}}=D+B
$$

$$
\text{New shares}\approx\frac{B}{S},\qquad V\_{\text{after}}\approx V+B
$$

Share quantities are rounded down to the supported precision. The actual resulting line must pass the health checks; the approximate formula is not a guaranteed executable quote.

The collateral-only upper bound on an additional draw is:

$$
B\le\max(0,M C-D)
$$

Actual availability can be lower because of joint risk, shared borrowing capacity, vault minimums, vault availability, pending withdrawals, or price readiness. The line must be Active, and positive bad debt on the account blocks new draws.

**Vault gains do not expand the collateral-based borrowing limit.** They can improve the line’s health, but you cannot repeatedly borrow against the value of the shares created by previous draws.

### How credit health works

Health evaluates **both collateral value and encumbered vault value relative to debt**. It also enforces an independent minimum collateral ratio.

For an ordinary line with positive debt, define:

$$
c=\frac{C}{D},\qquad v=\frac{V}{D}
$$

These ratios compare current values with current debt. They are not returns measured from the original deposit date.

The current launch uses these reference values:

| Collateral asset         | Admission ratio **M** | Collateral reference loss **X** | Conversion discount **d** | Insurance Fund inventory sale discount |
| ------------------------ | --------------------: | ------------------------------: | ------------------------: | -------------------------------------: |
| ADA                      |                  1.00 |                            0.30 |                        5% |                                     2% |
| SundaeSwap USDCx/USDM LP |                  1.00 |                            0.10 |                        1% |                                   0.5% |
| Aave V3 Ethereum aUSDC   |                  1.00 |                            0.05 |                     0.25% |                                   0.1% |

The shared parameters are:

| Parameter                        | Current launch value | Meaning                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------: | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Y**, vault reference loss      |                 0.20 | From C = V = D, a vault-value loss of 20% of debt reaches the joint recovery boundary if collateral value is unchanged. |
| **F**, collateral floor          |                 0.50 | An ordinary Active line must retain collateral value strictly greater than 50% of its debt.                             |
| **r**, recovery target parameter |                 0.05 | Sets the buffer required to finish recovery. It is not a fee or a fixed amount sold.                                    |

**X** has the equivalent meaning for collateral: from **C = V = D**, an ADA collateral-value loss of 30% of debt reaches the joint boundary if vault value stays equal to debt. It is not an automatic 30% reduction in ADA’s borrowing value, and it does not guarantee that every ADA line can withstand a 30% price fall. Simultaneous vault losses can bring recovery forward.

#### Joint risk

The vault contribution is:

$$
\Phi(v)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{1-v}{Y}, & v\le 1\\\[4pt]
1-v, & v>1
\end{cases}
$$

The line’s joint risk is:

$$
J=\frac{1-c}{X}+\Phi(v)
$$

When collateral and vault value are both below debt, the two loss contributions add together. Values above debt can provide a negative contribution, offsetting some risk. Vault surplus is treated differently from vault loss: the surplus contribution uses **1 − v**, without dividing by Y.

An ordinary line stays within the Active risk boundaries only when **both** conditions hold:

$$
J<1\quad\text{and}\quad c>F
$$

Recovery starts when **either** condition holds:

$$
J\ge1\quad\text{or}\quad c\le F
$$

Equality starts recovery. A draw or ordinary collateral release must also satisfy the admission limit described above.

#### Reading the displayed health score

The displayed components are:

$$
\text{Joint health}=100(2-J)
$$

$$
\text{Floor health}=100\frac{c}{F}
$$

$$
\text{Credit health}=\max\left(0,\min(\text{Joint health},\text{Floor health})\right)
$$

* **200** is the balanced reference, where C = V = D.
* **100** is the recovery entry boundary.
* Values below 100 can appear while recovery is being detected or processed.
* Values above 200 are possible.

These are **score points, not percentages**. A score of 150 does not mean a 150% return or a 50% price buffer. Scores are displayed to two decimal places; the unrounded conditions determine eligibility. A display rounded to 100.00 can therefore sit very close to either side of the boundary.

A debt remainder, bad debt, or missing required prices can leave the health score unavailable. Use the line’s stated status as well as its score. A line can remain in Recovery above 100 while it works toward the completion targets or finishes outstanding settlements.

#### ADA health examples

Each row below uses **D = $400**, **X = 0.30**, **Y = 0.20**, and **F = 0.50**. They are independent examples before any recovery settlement.

| Situation                                  |    C |    V | Joint risk J | Credit health | Result                   |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---: | ---: | -----------: | ------------: | ------------------------ |
| Balanced starting point                    | $400 | $400 |            0 |        200.00 | Within Active boundaries |
| Collateral loses 30%; vault unchanged      | $280 | $400 |            1 |        100.00 | Recovery boundary        |
| Vault loses 20%; collateral unchanged      | $400 | $320 |            1 |        100.00 | Recovery boundary        |
| Collateral loses 15%; vault loses 10%      | $340 | $360 |            1 |        100.00 | Recovery boundary        |
| Vault surplus supports lower collateral    | $250 | $500 |            1 |        100.00 | Recovery boundary        |
| Collateral floor binds despite vault gains | $200 | $800 |          2/3 |        100.00 | Recovery boundary        |

For the simultaneous-loss example:

$$
J=\frac{1-340/400}{0.30}+\frac{1-360/400}{0.20}
\=0.50+0.50=1
$$

For the profitable-vault example:

$$
J=\frac{1-250/400}{0.30}+(1-500/400)
\=1.25-0.25=1
$$

For the collateral-floor example, c = 0.50. Recovery begins even though joint risk is below 1, because the collateral floor is an independent requirement.

#### Is there one ADA liquidation price?

The trigger depends on vault value and debt as well as ADA’s price. If **V stays equal to D**, the ADA joint boundary is:

$$
C=(1-X)D=0.70D
$$

For 800 pledged ADA and $400 debt:

$$
P\_{\text{boundary}}=\frac{0.70\times400}{800}=$0.35
$$

This $0.35 example is valid only while debt stays $400 and vault value stays $400. If the vault falls to $360, the joint boundary instead occurs at C = $340, or **$0.425 per ADA**. Repayments, additional collateral, and vault performance all change the boundary.

### Repaying debt and releasing ADA

You can repay using spendable USD in your account. For a payment A:

$$
\text{Debt repaid}=\min(A,D)
$$

$$
D\_{\text{after}}=D-\text{Debt repaid}
$$

Adding ADA to custody does not itself repay debt. Pledging more ADA increases collateral value; a USD repayment reduces debt.

To release **u** ADA from an ordinary Active line, the remaining collateral must pass both admission and health checks:

$$
C\_{\text{after}}=(q-u)P
$$

$$
D\le M C\_{\text{after}},\qquad J\_{\text{after}}<1,\qquad \frac{C\_{\text{after}}}{D}>F
$$

For example, with 800 pledged ADA at $0.50, $300 debt, and $400 of encumbered vault value, the admission limit requires at least $300 of collateral. That is **600 ADA**. Releasing **200 ADA** leaves C = $300 and V = $400; it also passes the health checks at the stated terms.

Recovery blocks new draws and collateral releases. Direct repayment and additional pledges remain available. When debt reaches zero, the line closes, its remaining collateral becomes available custody, and its remaining shares become unencumbered. Normal vault and on-chain withdrawal requirements still apply.

### Withdrawing vault shares

A withdrawal can contain unencumbered shares, shares assigned to a particular credit line, or both. The selected sources are recorded when you request it so each line receives the correct debt repayment.

Ordinary withdrawal requests follow the vault’s lock period and execution requirements. The share price when the withdrawal executes determines the proceeds. A quoted value at request time is not a guaranteed payout; the vault’s performance and any required trading to free liquidity can change it.

For an ordinary SLP withdrawal of **n** shares at final share price **S**, proceeds are:

$$
G=nS
$$

SLP charges zero vault fees, so there is no vault-fee deduction. For shares assigned to a line, the order is **linked debt repayment → your remaining USD**:

$$
R=\min(G,D),\qquad U=G-R,\qquad D\_{\text{after}}=D-R
$$

Here R is the amount repaid and U is the USD paid to you. For unencumbered SLP shares, proceeds are paid to you without a linked credit repayment.

#### Profitable withdrawal

Assume your $400 draw bought 400 shares at $1.00 each. You withdraw all 400 when S = $1.20, with $400 of debt still outstanding:

| Calculation                   |  Amount |
| ----------------------------- | ------: |
| Gross: 400 × $1.20            |    $480 |
| Profit: 400 × ($1.20 − $1.00) |     $80 |
| Debt repaid                   |    $400 |
| USD paid to you               | **$80** |
| Remaining debt                |      $0 |

#### Withdrawal that leaves debt

Assume the same 400 shares are instead redeemed at S = $0.90, with $400 of debt:

| Calculation        |  Amount |
| ------------------ | ------: |
| Gross: 400 × $0.90 |    $360 |
| Debt repaid        |    $360 |
| USD paid to you    |  **$0** |
| Remaining debt     | **$40** |

A voluntary withdrawal must also leave an eligible line. A partial withdrawal that would leave an ordinary Active line outside its health boundaries is rejected. A final-share withdrawal that leaves debt requires the specific confirmation and collateral lock described next.

### The 24-hour debt remainder

If you voluntarily redeem the last encumbered shares while debt would remain, you must explicitly confirm that outcome and retain enough collateral. Without that confirmation and collateral, the withdrawal cannot settle in this form.

An accepted debt remainder has positive debt, zero encumbered shares, and a fixed **24-hour deadline beginning when the remainder is created**. It temporarily remains Active under special rules. The ordinary joint-health formula does not govern this exception, and no normal health score is displayed.

For remaining debt **Dᵣ**, the required fair collateral value is:

$$
C\_{\text{lock}}=\max\left(
\frac{D\_r}{(1-d)(1-X)},\ F D\_r,\ \frac{D\_r}{M}
\right)
$$

The first term retains enough collateral to cover debt after applying the collateral reference loss and the conversion discount. The other terms preserve the collateral floor and admission requirement.

For ADA, using Dᵣ = $40, d = 0.05, X = 0.30, F = 0.50, and M = 1.00:

$$
C\_{\text{lock}}=\max\left(\frac{40}{0.95\times0.70},20,40\right)
\=$60.15037594\ldots
$$

At $0.50 per ADA:

$$
q\_{\text{lock}}=\frac{60.15037594\ldots}{0.50}
\=120.30075188\ldots\text{ ADA}
$$

Rounded up to six decimal places, at least **120.300752 ADA** must remain allocated. The lock is recalculated using current prices and settings. A price decline can make the retained amount insufficient; this calculation does not guarantee future sale proceeds or payer liquidity.

During the remainder, you can repay debt or add collateral. Before the deadline and before closing starts, a permitted new draw into the same vault can end the remainder by creating shares and restoring an ordinary Active line. That draw increases debt and must satisfy all normal checks. Excess collateral can be released only while the special lock and deadline rules permit it.

You may request closing earlier. Otherwise, closing begins when the expired deadline is processed. Closing opens a single **30-second payer period** for collateral conversion. During that period, another eligible account can pay USD to reduce debt and receive discounted collateral.

At or after the payer deadline, the next eligible fresh-price evaluation applies Insurance Fund conversion to the remaining debt and collateral. Any debt still left becomes bad debt. Missing prices can delay settlement; they do not reset the deadline or reopen borrowing. The 30-second period is a conversion period, not an extension of your borrowing window.

### What happens during automatic recovery?

Automatic recovery reduces the line’s debt after joint risk reaches 1 or the collateral ratio reaches the floor. A falling vault value can trigger recovery even when ADA’s price has not changed. Health is reassessed as accepted prices and relevant financial state are processed.

Recovery can use two sources:

1. **Encumbered vault shares.** Strike can redeem some of the shares assigned to the line and use the net proceeds to reduce its debt.
2. **Allocated collateral.** An eligible payer can buy collateral at the configured conversion discount, with the payment reducing the line’s debt.

There is no fixed percentage split. The process first seeks a sufficient vault settlement that can preserve the vault’s trading positions. Otherwise, it can combine available vault settlement with funded collateral conversion, seeking to limit collateral consumption.

When funded conversion can improve the line, it receives a **30-second priority period** before forced unwinding of vault trading positions becomes eligible. Vault settlements that do not require such an unwind can still occur during that period. The period is not a promise that the user has 30 seconds before any recovery action.

Automatic recovery uses its own settlement process. The ordinary user withdrawal lock period does not delay it. Recovery can take priority over pending requests and use the encumbered shares reserved in them; a pending withdrawal does not protect those shares from recovery.

Settlements remain subject to current prices, available vault capacity, execution limits, and actual market liquidity. Recovery may require multiple settlements. A temporary liquidity or execution limit does not by itself authorize immediate Insurance Fund use or establish a completion time.

#### ADA collateral conversion

If P is the accepted ADA price and d is the conversion discount:

$$
P\_{\text{conversion}}=P(1-d)
$$

At P = $0.50 and d = 5%:

$$
P\_{\text{conversion}}=0.50\times0.95=$0.475
$$

For a permitted conversion of 100 ADA:

$$
\text{Payer payment}=100\times0.475=$47.50
$$

The payer spends $47.50 and receives 100 ADA in custody. Your line gives up 100 ADA and its debt falls by $47.50, assuming at least that much debt remains. Conversion size is limited by the authorized recovery amount, available collateral, payer funds, and rounding.

The discount means $50 of marked collateral in this example repays $47.50 of debt. It is an economic cost of conversion. Any small payment surplus caused by final rounding is credited to you after the remaining debt is cleared.

#### Costs when recovery sells vault shares

If recovery must unwind vault trading positions, execution can reduce the vault’s share price. Additional recovery withholding can also allocate forced execution loss to the shares being settled. This withholding is a loss allocation, not a fixed percentage fee.

For a recovery settlement, let **W** be that additional withholding:

$$
G=nS,\qquad N=G-W,\qquad R=\min(N,D)
$$

The final share price already reflects the vault’s state after execution; W represents the additional allocated withholding. The amount available to repay debt is **N**, not the original quoted value of the shares.

#### When recovery finishes

Full repayment finishes recovery and closes the line. A line with positive debt must meet stricter completion targets and have no outstanding recovery settlement that can still affect its finances.

The targets are derived from X, F, and r:

$$
J^*=\frac{1-r/X}{1-r},\qquad F^*=\frac{F}{1-r}
$$

Positive-debt completion requires:

$$
J\le J^*\quad\text{and}\quad\frac{C}{D}\ge F^*
$$

For ADA:

$$
J^\*=\frac{1-0.05/0.30}{0.95}=\frac{50}{57}\approx0.877193
$$

$$
F^\*=\frac{0.50}{0.95}=\frac{10}{19}\approx0.526316
$$

The corresponding ADA health threshold is approximately **112.28 for the joint component** and **105.26 for the floor component**. Both exact targets must pass. There is no single displayed score that substitutes for these two checks and settlement completion.

The 5% parameter sets these targets. It does not mean that exactly 5% of every line is sold or that recovery costs 5%.

### Insurance Fund and bad debt

For ordinary recovery, the Insurance Fund is a backstop after a current assessment establishes that the normal funded conversion and permitted vault settlement routes are exhausted and no conflicting settlement remains. Elapsed time alone is insufficient. The confirmed debt remainder follows its separate closing schedule above.

Insurance Fund conversion uses the applicable collateral conversion discount and the collateral amount needed under the settlement and rounding rules. The Fund receives the converted collateral as inventory.

If debt remains after that backstop settlement, it is classified as bad debt. **Bad debt is not forgiven.** It remains visible, can be repaid with spendable USD, and blocks new credit draws while positive. Repayments of classified bad debt go to the Insurance Fund.

The Insurance Fund’s inventory can later be sold to eligible buyers. That is a separate transaction with its own sale discount:

$$
P\_{\text{inventory sale}}=P(1-d\_{\text{sale}})
$$

With ADA at $0.50 and the current 2% inventory sale discount:

$$
P\_{\text{inventory sale}}=0.50\times0.98=$0.49
$$

A buyer purchasing 100 ADA pays $49 and receives 100 ADA in custody. The inventory sale does not reduce the original borrower’s debt a second time.

### Prices, fees, and practical limits

**ADA valuation.** ADA collateral uses the accepted direct ADA/USD spot index. ADA quantity stays in ADA; only its USD valuation changes. The current maximum accepted price age is 10 seconds. LP prices have a two-minute maximum age, and scaled aUSDC prices have a 60-second maximum age.

**Price interruptions.** Draws, collateral releases, conversions, and terminal recovery settlement require the complete current set of supported collateral prices. A missing price for another supported asset can therefore pause these actions on an ADA line. Repayment and additional collateral pledges remain available without that complete set. An unavailable valuation is not treated as an asset price of zero.

**aUSDC accounting.** Aave V3 Ethereum aUSDC is tracked in scaled units so its value can reflect the Aave liquidity index. If I is the index expressed as a multiplier, aUSDC units = scaled units × I, and the USD price per scaled unit = I × the USDC/USD price. This accounting differs from ADA’s fixed six-decimal unit conversion.

**Fees and borrowing charges.** SLP’s vault fee is 0%. The current credit mechanics also do not accrue time-based borrowing interest or add a separate origination fee to a draw. Debt increases by the USD drawn and decreases through settled repayment. Vault performance, trading and funding costs reflected in share value, conversion discounts, recovery execution losses, and applicable transfer or network costs can still affect the outcome. On-chain transfers follow the costs shown in the current transaction quote.

**Timing.** An ordinary line has no fixed repayment maturity in these mechanics, but its health is continuously subject to reassessment. The 24-hour limit applies specifically to a confirmed debt remainder. Vault withdrawal lock periods and on-chain settlement times are separate.

**Precision.** ADA custody uses six decimal places. Partial credit debt movements use up to eight USD decimal places, and small partial debt reductions round down. Required collateral locks round up to the asset’s precision. Full repayment can clear the exact outstanding debt. Very small requests can be rejected when rounding would produce no valid shares or debt reduction.

**Capacity and liquidity.** Supported collateral does not guarantee that a new draw is available. Asset-wide and product-wide debt limits can restrict borrowing, and SLP must be accepting deposits. A healthy line or a displayed vault value does not guarantee immediate cash withdrawal. Internal USD issuance, asset valuations, and expected future recovery proceeds are not settled external liquidity.

### Common questions

**Do I keep my ADA exposure?** Yes, for ADA still held in your custody. Its USD value can rise or fall. ADA converted during recovery leaves your custody.

**Does an ADA deposit earn vault returns automatically?** No. Vault exposure begins when a draw buys vault shares. Merely depositing or pledging ADA does not create those shares.

**Can I use the same ADA twice?** No. Each pledged unit is allocated to one line. Available custody is reduced by all of your allocations in that asset.

**Can a vault loss trigger recovery while ADA is stable?** Yes. Vault value is part of joint risk. At the balanced reference, a 20% vault-value loss reaches the boundary even with unchanged collateral.

**Does recovery always sell ADA first?** No. It can use vault shares, collateral conversion, or both according to the line’s needs and executable liquidity.

**Does selling all my vault shares automatically settle everything?** No. Net proceeds may be below debt. A voluntary final-share withdrawal that leaves debt requires confirmation and enough retained collateral for a debt remainder.

**What happens after I repay everything?** The line closes. Remaining collateral becomes available custody, and remaining vault shares become unencumbered. You can then use the normal withdrawal flows for each.\
\
**Does the one-year SLP loss coverage program cover this?** Yes, but it only covers losses on vault shares. It does not cover losses caused by a decline in ADA’s price, including losses from liquidation triggered by that decline.


# Points

Deposit into the SLP vault to earn points every day. At the end of each season, your points convert into STRIKE, paid on Cardano.

**Season 1:** Sep 28, 00:00 UTC – Oct 28, 00:00 UTC, 2026 (30 days) · 20,000 STRIKE prize pool · 888 points a day

### How it works

1. **Deposit into SLP.** Any amount, any time during the season.
2. **Earn points daily.** Every UTC day, 888 points are split between all depositors based on their time-weighted average deposit.
3. **Get STRIKE at season end.** Your points convert into your share of the prize pool and are sent to your Cardano payout address.

### Time-weighted average

Your deposit is averaged over each day by how long you held it.

> Example: $1,000 deposited for the first 12 hours and $3,000 for the last 12 hours = **$2,000** time-weighted average for that day.

Your points for the day:

```
daily points × your average deposit ÷ all depositors' average deposits
```

> Example: your average is $2,000 and all depositors total $400,000 → 888 × 2,000 ÷ 400,000 = **4.44 points**.

Points update every hour. Today's points are an estimate until the day ends, then they're final.

### Converting to STRIKE

The rate is fixed for the whole season:

```
season points = 888 points a day × 30 days = 26,640
STRIKE per point = 20,000 STRIKE ÷ 26,640 ≈ 0.7508
your STRIKE = your points × 0.7508
```

> Example: 100 points × 0.7508 ≈ **75.08 STRIKE**.

### Payout address

STRIKE is paid on Cardano.

* **Cardano wallet accounts** are paid to their wallet automatically.
* **Ethereum, Solana and email accounts** set a Cardano address (`addr1…`) on the Points page. It can only be set once and can't be changed.

### Coming soon

Trading will earn points in a future season.

### FAQ

**Do I need to claim points?** No. They're added automatically every day you have a deposit.

**Do vault profits or losses change my points?** No. Points are based on the amount you deposited, not its current value.

**What doesn't earn points?** Shares you've requested to withdraw, and deposits made with USD borrowed through Borrow & Earn.

**Do sub-account deposits count?** Yes. They're added to your main account.

**Why did my points for today go down?** Today's points are an estimate. If others deposit during the day, your share gets smaller. Past days never change.

**Does withdrawing remove points I've earned?** No. You keep them. Withdrawn funds just stop earning.

**Can I change my payout address?** No. It's locked once set, so double-check it.

**Can I transfer points?** No. Points are non-transferable and may be adjusted for wash trading or abuse.


# Clan Competitions

Clan competitions are timed team events on Strike. You join (or create) a **clan**, trade during the event window, and compete for a shared **prize pool**. Clans are ranked by combined trading volume; top clans split the pool, and each clan splits its share among members.

### How to participate

You must be in a clan **before the roster lock** for your trading to count toward that event.

**Option A — Join a clan**

1. Browse clans and pick one with open spots.
2. Join the clan directly — no chief approval required.

**Option B — Create a clan**

1. Create a new clan and become its chief.
2. You may need a minimum lifetime trading volume to create a clan (check the app for the current requirement).

**Rules**

* One account can belong to **one clan at a time**.
* You cannot join a clan while you already belong to one, or while you already own a clan.
* Each clan has a member cap.
* Only one competition runs at a time.

### Event timeline

Each competition has three important dates (all UTC):

| Phase           | What it means                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Start**       | Competition begins; trading volume starts counting.                                                                                              |
| **Roster lock** | Deadline to be on a clan roster with full credit. Members who join **after** this date stay on the clan but earn **zero** volume for that event. |
| **End**         | Competition closes; final rankings and prizes are calculated.                                                                                    |

Between **roster lock** and **end**, members **cannot leave** and chiefs **cannot kick** anyone. Before roster lock, members may leave freely; chiefs cannot leave their own clan yet.

### How scoring works

Your score comes from **trading volume during the event** (from start to end).

* **External volume** — trades against traders outside your clan — counts fully.
* **Internal volume** — trades against other members of your clan — counts at a reduced rate (only half of that volume is credited).

Each member’s credited volume is added together for the clan total. Clans are ranked on the **leaderboard** by this total; higher is better.

### Prizes

When an event ends:

1. The prize pool is split among **top-ranked clans** according to that event’s payout tiers (for example, 1st place 40%, 2nd 25%, and so on).
2. Each winning clan’s share is then split among its members:
   * The **chief** receives a fixed lead commission (typically 10% of the clan’s share).
   * The rest is divided among **all members** (including the chief) in proportion to each member’s credited volume.

Members who joined after roster lock receive no share from that event’s volume-based split.

Prize amounts and asset type are shown on each event in the app. Past results and per-member payouts are available after settlement.

### Tips

* Join a clan **well before roster lock**.
* More active traders in a clan means more combined volume — but trading only with teammates earns less credit than trading with outsiders.
* Check the **leaderboard** during the event to track your clan’s rank and projected rewards.


# Sub-accounts

Sub-accounts let you create separate trading accounts under one master account. Each sub-account can have its own balance, positions, orders, performance, and risk level.

Your master account remains the main account connected to your wallet. Sub-accounts are managed by the master account and do not have their own separate wallet identity.

### Why use sub-accounts?

Sub-accounts help you keep different activities separate without needing to manage multiple wallets.

* Run different trading strategies independently.
* Separate hedging positions from your main trading strategy.
* Give each strategy its own balance and risk budget.
* Track performance and PnL by strategy.
* Keep market-making, arbitrage, and directional trading separate.
* Test new ideas with a dedicated balance.

Each sub-account has its own margin and liquidation risk. Balances and risk are not automatically combined across your master account and sub-accounts.

### Moving funds between accounts

Funds can be moved internally between your master account and its sub-accounts.

You can:

* Move funds from the master account into a sub-account.
* Move funds from a sub-account back to the master account.
* Move funds between sub-accounts belonging to the same master account.

These internal transfers do not involve the blockchain and do not require an external wallet transaction.

Only accounts belonging to the same master account can transfer funds to one another. Transfers between different users are not supported.

### Deposits and withdrawals

External deposits and withdrawals are handled through the master account.

Sub-accounts do not have their own deposit addresses and cannot directly withdraw funds to an external wallet. To move funds out of a sub-account, first transfer the funds back to the master account. The master account can then complete the external withdrawal.

### Vaults

Only the master account can deposit funds into or withdraw funds from a vault.

Sub-accounts cannot directly:

* Deposit into a vault.
* Request a withdrawal from a vault.
* Use a vault position as a substitute for their own trading balance.

The usual flow is:

1. Deposit external funds into the master account.
2. Use the master account to deposit funds into a vault.
3. Receive vault shares in the master account.
4. Request a withdrawal from the master account when you want to exit the vault.
5. After the vault's lock-up period, the withdrawn funds return to the master account.
6. Transfer those funds to a sub-account if they are needed for trading.

Vault withdrawals are based on the number of shares held and may be subject to a lock-up period. A vault withdrawal returns funds to the master account; it is not an immediate external wallet withdrawal.

### Hedging example

A trader wants to run a BTC strategy while reducing its overall market exposure.

They can create two sub-accounts:

* **BTC Directional:** holds the main long BTC position.
* **BTC Hedge:** holds a short BTC position to offset some of the directional exposure.

The master account can allocate funds to both sub-accounts and monitor their performance separately. This makes it easier to see how much profit or loss comes from the main strategy and how much comes from the hedge.

The hedge reduces overall exposure, but margin is still calculated separately for each sub-account. The hedge account must maintain enough collateral for its own position.

### Other examples

#### Market making and directional trading

Use one sub-account for market-making orders and another for directional trades. This keeps inventory, fills, and strategy performance easier to review.

#### Multiple independent strategies

Use separate sub-accounts for trend following, mean reversion, arbitrage, and other strategies. A problem in one strategy does not automatically close positions in another sub-account.

#### Testing and experimentation

Allocate a small balance to a new strategy without mixing its activity with your main trading account.

### Important rules

* The master account owns and manages its sub-accounts.
* Sub-accounts do not have independent wallet identities.
* External deposits and withdrawals are master-account-only.
* Vault deposits and withdrawals are master-account-only.
* Internal transfers are limited to the master account and its own sub-accounts.
* Sub-accounts cannot create additional sub-accounts.
* Margin and liquidation risk are managed separately for each account.


# Copy Trading

Copy trading mirrors a lead trader on your Strike account. Pick a lead — a Hyperliquid wallet or a Strike trader — choose how trades are sized, and Strike places matching market orders on your account whenever that lead executes a trade.

* Copying starts immediately when you subscribe.
* One active subscription per lead. Stop and subscribe again to restart.
* You can copy Hyperliquid wallets (0x…) and Strike traders.
* Saved traders are bookmarks only — saving does not copy.

### What gets copied

* Executed fills only, not resting orders. When the lead cancels an unfilled order there is nothing to cancel on your side.
* Copies are market IOC orders on Strike — same side, reduce-only when the lead's fill is reduce-only.
* **Hyperliquid leads:** only markets listed and tradable on Strike (HL BTC → BTC-USD, HL xyz:NVDA → NVDA-USD). Unlisted markets and unsupported HIP-3 contracts are skipped.
* **Strike leads:** every Strike market the lead trades, including fills of their limit orders and TP/SL.
* **Lead liquidations and ADL:** when the lead's position is liquidated or auto-deleveraged, your copy closes by the same fraction. See How closes are sized.
* Only fills after you subscribe, unless you turn on **Copy open positions**.

Hyperliquid copies usually land within seconds. Under heavy load they can take up to about a minute; Strike catches up automatically. Strike-lead copies are typically faster, since they come straight from Strike's own fill stream.

**Not copied:** grid bot and TWAP orders, orders a Strike lead places as a copier of someone else, vault accounts, activity from before you subscribed, orders that never fill.

### Copy modes

Minimum copy amounts may apply — check the app for current limits.

#### Fixed ratio

Set a copy amount (e.g. $5,000). It is reserved while the subscription is active, and every lead opening is copied at the same fraction of the lead's account:

```
copy ratio = copy amount ÷ lead's account value   (capped at 100%)
your size  = lead's fill size × copy ratio
```

Lead's account value is their Hyperliquid account value, or for a Strike lead their Strike account equity (cross plus isolated margin balances).

> Lead has $100,000 and buys 0.1 BTC. With a $5,000 copy amount your ratio is 5%, so you buy 0.005 BTC.

* Copy amount is not a spend budget. Copies do not reduce it, and the ratio is recomputed on every fill.
* If the lead's account is much larger than your copy amount, sizes can round to zero or fall below the market minimum; those copies are skipped. Increase the copy amount or use fixed amount.

#### Fixed amount

Set a margin per entry: the initial margin each distinct lead order targets, at your current leverage on that market.

```
target notional = margin per entry × your leverage
your size       = target notional ÷ entry price
```

> $50 margin at 10x ETH-USD leverage, lead sells ETH at $3,000: $500 notional, about 0.1666 ETH.

* One copy per lead order (Hyperliquid or Strike), however many partial fills it has. Each new lead order targets the full margin again.
* Your available balance must cover the full margin per entry, or that entry is skipped — it is not sized down. If no market-valid size remains (min/max size, lot step, min notional) the copy is also skipped.
* Margin per entry is a sizing input, not a loss cap. In cross margin, losses can exceed it.
* No lump-sum reservation. Total exposure is limited only by your available equity and max margin per symbol, if set.

In either mode, a copy that fails (insufficient margin, size rules, engine rejection) does not stop the subscription — later fills still try.

### How closes are sized

Same in both modes and for both lead types: each lead closing fill closes the same fraction of your copied position that it closes of the lead's.

```
lead close fraction = lead close size ÷ lead position before the close   (capped at 100%)
your close size     = your copied size × lead close fraction
```

A full lead close closes your whole copied position, regardless of price or leverage changes since entry. Manual size and other subscriptions' size in the same market are untouched.

This includes the lead being liquidated or auto-deleveraged. Each liquidation fill is a lead close, so a partial liquidation closes the same fraction of your copy and a full liquidation closes all of it. The subscription stays active.

### Advanced settings

Optional, both modes, Hyperliquid and Strike leads alike.

* **Max margin per symbol** — caps the margin one subscription can hold in any single market. An entry that would go over the cap is skipped, not sized down. Closes are never blocked.
* **Asset filter** — list markets the subscription must never open (e.g. BTC-USD, DOGE-USD). Closes on those markets are still mirrored, so an existing copy position closes with the lead.
* **Copy open positions** — at subscribe time, mirror the positions the lead already holds, sized like a new entry at mark price. Positions that fail a check are skipped and show as failed in copy order history. One-time only.

### Leverage and margin mode

* Copies use your Strike leverage and margin mode on each market, never the lead's.
* The first trade on a market, copy or manual, locks in that market's settings. Changing leverage or margin mode later affects only future copies; open positions are not resized or re-levered.
* The account default margin mode starts as cross. Switching it to isolated affects only markets you have not traded yet; existing markets keep their own mode.
* Each sub-account has its own default and starts on cross. To open new copied markets isolated, set the default before the first copy.

### Reserved balance

* Fixed-ratio copy amounts are reserved in full while the subscription is active. Reserved funds count against available balance: no withdrawals, manual trading, or other fixed-ratio subscriptions against them.
* With $20,000, copying Lead A at $5,000 and Lead B at $3,000 leaves $12,000 available; a third $15,000 subscription is rejected.
* The reservation is released when you stop.
* Liquidation, ADL, or a bankrupt close does not release it and does not stop copying — that market's copy PnL is booked and the subscription stays active.
* **Strike leads only:** the profit share you would owe the lead is also held from your available balance — 10% of positive realized copy PnL while active, until it is paid on stop.

### Copying Strike traders

* Find Strike traders in Discover (Strike or All platform). Search by nickname, account ID, or wallet address.
* Sizing, closes, leverage, and advanced settings work exactly as for Hyperliquid leads.
* **Profit share** — when you stop a Strike-lead subscription in profit, 10% of that profit is paid to the lead. Your stopped PnL shows what you kept. Losses are not shared, and Hyperliquid leads take no share.
* You cannot copy yourself, your own sub-accounts, or a vault.

**For Strike leads** — your lead dashboard shows, per day and today:

* Active copiers and unique followers
* Volume copied from your trades
* Profit share earned from stopped subscriptions, plus live unrealized share from active copiers
* Each profit share received: copier address, nickname, avatar, their PnL, amount, and sizing

### Managing subscriptions

* **Subscribe** — pick a lead, choose a mode, set the copy amount or margin per entry, confirm. You cannot copy yourself, your sub-accounts, or a vault, and sizing must fit within available balance.
* **Use a sub-account** — copy from a dedicated sub-account funded with only what you are willing to risk, so losses stay isolated. Set its default margin mode before the first copy.
* **Update** — change the copy amount (increases need extra available balance), margin per entry, max margin per symbol, or asset filter at any time. Open positions are not resized.
* **Stop** — copying halts immediately. Copied open positions are closed with market reduce-only orders for the size attributed to this subscription; manual size in the same market is untouched. Resting copied orders are not canceled. The reservation is released, and for a Strike lead any profit share is paid. Stop is safe to retry if a close fails partway.

A subscription only stops when you stop it. Liquidations, of your positions or the lead's, never stop copying.

### Tracking

* **Orders** — every copied order, the lead that triggered it, and its status. Copied orders also appear in your normal order history.
* **Positions** — attributed to the lead that opened them. Size, margin, and PnL reflect the net copied size for that subscription, not the full live position if you also trade the market manually. A manual close consumes copy-attributed size first, split proportionally across subscriptions in the same direction, and realized PnL is credited in the same proportion. Before sizing a lead close or a stop, Strike waits for attribution records to catch up with every fill on the position; if they do not within a short timeout, that close is skipped and logged rather than sized from stale data.
* **Dashboard** — mode and sizing, reserved amount or margin per entry, total margin, position worth, realized and total PnL.

### Discover traders

Discover lists Hyperliquid leaderboard traders and Strike traders — filter by platform: Hyperliquid, Strike, or All.

Hyperliquid profiles are enriched with:

* **Traded assets** from the last 2,000 fills — top five by notional, plus how many days that window covers.
* **Trading style** (inactive, market maker, algo, scalper, day, swing, position, unknown) from fill rate, maker share, and median hold time, and **bias** (long, short, neutral) from opening notional.
* **Copy score** (0–100) for 7-day, 30-day, and all-time windows, weighting ROI, PnL consistency, drawdown, profit factor, recent activity, share of volume on Strike-tradable markets, traded asset diversity, and account size (very large accounts score lower because their fills are harder to mirror). A recommended direction — copy, counter, or none — is derived from it.
* **Recommended copy amount** for fixed ratio: the smallest amount at which at least 80% of the trader's recent opening-fill notional would have produced valid Strike orders. It is a total allocation, not per trade, and is historical guidance only.

Filter by address or name search, top-N rank (applied before other filters), assets, style, bias, account value, PnL, volume, minimum copy score, and minimum Strike-copyable share. The Hyperliquid leaderboard refreshes about every 15 minutes; profiles refresh about twice a day, with active leads and top-ranked traders first.

### FAQ

**Can I copy the same trader again after stopping?** Yes. Stop the current subscription, then subscribe again.

**Can I copy a Strike trader?** Yes. Pick them in Discover and subscribe like any other lead. When you stop a profitable Strike-lead subscription, 10% of that profit is paid to the lead.

**Do Strike leads see who is copying them?** They see copier counts, copied volume, and profit share on their lead dashboard. Each profit share they receive shows that copier's address, nickname, and avatar.

**Do copied orders show up in my normal order history?** Yes. They appear as regular orders on your account, linked to the copy subscription that created them.

**What happens if I don't have enough margin for one copy?** For fixed amount, the entry is skipped if your available balance is below the full margin per entry. With enough margin, if the size is zero or breaks the market's minimum size, maximum size, or minimum notional rules, it is skipped. A concurrent balance change can still make the matching engine reject the order. The subscription stays active and later fills still try.

**Does copy stop if my positions are liquidated?** No. Liquidation, ADL, or a bankrupt close of your positions does not stop copying. That market's copy PnL is booked and the subscription stays active, so other copy positions and later lead fills still copy. A subscription only stops when you stop it.

**What happens if the lead is liquidated?** Your copy of that position closes with the lead's, by the same fraction — a partial liquidation closes part of your copy, a full liquidation closes all of it. The subscription stays active and later lead fills keep copying.

**Can I copy a vault?** No. Vault accounts cannot be followed via copy trading.

**Can I use a sub-account for copy trading?** Yes. Subscriptions can be scoped to a sub-account. This is the recommended way to copy trade. You still cannot copy your own primary account or another sub-account in the same family.

**Why did my copy arrive late?** Copies are usually near real-time. Hyperliquid copies can occasionally take up to about a minute during heavy activity or connectivity issues. Strike catches up automatically.

**If the lead's order fills in many small pieces, how many copies do I get?** With fixed ratio, fills of the same order that arrive together are combined into one proportional copy; later pieces are copied separately. With fixed amount, one margin-sized copy per lead opening order. Closing fills close the matching fraction of your copied position in both modes.

**Whose leverage does fixed amount use?** Yours, not the lead's. If you already set leverage on that market, copies use it. If you have never set that market, Strike uses the market's default (typically 10x). Changing your leverage later only affects new copied entries.

**Whose margin mode do copied trades use?** Yours, not the lead's. If you already set margin mode (or traded) on that market, copies use it. If you have never traded that market, copies use your account default margin mode, which starts as cross.

**Does $50 margin per entry cap my loss at $50?** No. It is the target initial margin used to size the entry. In cross margin, losses can exceed it.

**What happens when the lead adds to an existing symbol?** Each distinct opening or increase order targets the configured margin per entry again, if available balance, max margin per symbol, and engine risk checks allow it.
