# Websocket

Receive public, real-time changes to every visible resting order in the Strike order book. Use this stream with the L3 HTTP snapshot to reconstruct exact price levels and FIFO order priority.

### General information

Base endpoints:

| Environment | WebSocket                                      | Snapshot API                                              |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mainnet     | `wss://api.strikefinance.org/ws/l3`            | `https://api.strikefinance.org/v2/l3/snapshot`            |
| Testnet     | `wss://api-v2-testnet.strikefinance.org/ws/l3` | `https://api-v2-testnet.strikefinance.org/v2/l3/snapshot` |

* L3 market data is public. Do not send `session.logon`; no API wallet, scope is required.
* The channel name is `{lowercase-symbol}@l3`, for example `btc-usd@l3`. Subscription channel matching is case-insensitive.
* The initial enabled symbol is `BTC-USD`. Unsupported channels are rejected.
* Decimal values such as price and size are strings. `sequence`, `trade_id`, and timestamps are JSON numbers.
* Timestamps are Unix epoch milliseconds.
* Each WebSocket text frame contains exactly one JSON message. Unlike the user data stream, L3 messages are not newline-batched.
* The server sends WebSocket protocol ping frames every 54 seconds and requires a pong within 60 seconds. Standard WebSocket libraries normally reply automatically.
* There is no JSON `ping` method on this endpoint. A message such as `{"method":"ping"}` is rejected as an unsupported method.

Current public safety limits are 10 combined snapshot requests and WebSocket handshakes per second per source IP, 10 concurrent WebSocket connections per source IP, 10 symbol subscriptions per connection, and 4 KiB per inbound WebSocket message. Limits may change as the service evolves.

### Subscribe

Send a `SUBSCRIBE` command after the connection opens:

```json
{
  "method": "SUBSCRIBE",
  "params": ["btc-usd@l3"],
  "id": 1
}
```

The method name must be uppercase. `params` must contain at least one enabled L3 channel. Multiple channels may be supplied in one command, up to the per-connection limit. Duplicate or already-active subscriptions have no additional effect.

Successful acknowledgement:

```json
{
  "result": null,
  "id": 1
}
```

The `id` may be any JSON string or number and is echoed in the acknowledgement. An update can race with the acknowledgement, so start buffering `l3_update` messages as soon as the subscription command is sent. Distinguish command responses by the presence of `result` or `error`; market-data messages have `type: "l3_update"`.

### Unsubscribe

```json
{
  "method": "UNSUBSCRIBE",
  "params": ["btc-usd@l3"],
  "id": 2
}
```

Successful acknowledgement:

```json
{
  "result": null,
  "id": 2
}
```

Unsubscribing from a channel that is not active has no effect. Closing the socket stops all subscriptions.

### Incremental update

Every event represents one logical mutation of one symbol's visible order book:

```json
{
  "type": "l3_update",
  "symbol": "BTC-USD",
  "action": "partial_fill",
  "order_id": "YL8wLzJfqGW_uIZ7qvzu5A",
  "taker_order_id": "8CfeN3BBBOJLhNIx5ekcVw",
  "side": "buy",
  "price": "117500.00",
  "delta_size": "-0.04",
  "remaining_size": "0.11",
  "sequence": 918275,
  "trade_id": 771829,
  "timestamp": 1785480000123
}
```

#### Fields

| Field            | Type    | Presence      | Description                                                                               |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`           | string  | Always        | Message discriminator. Always `l3_update`.                                                |
| `symbol`         | string  | Always        | Canonical hyphen-separated market symbol.                                                 |
| `action`         | string  | Always        | `open`, `modify`, `cancel`, `partial_fill`, `full_fill`, or `clear`.                      |
| `order_id`       | string  | Order actions | Opaque public ID of the visible resting order being changed.                              |
| `taker_order_id` | string  | Fill actions  | Opaque public ID of the taking order that caused the fill.                                |
| `side`           | string  | Order actions | Resting order side: `buy` or `sell`.                                                      |
| `price`          | string  | Order actions | Resting order price.                                                                      |
| `delta_size`     | string  | Order actions | Signed change in visible size. Positive for `open`; negative for reductions and removals. |
| `remaining_size` | string  | Order actions | Visible size after applying the event. Terminal removals use `"0"`.                       |
| `sequence`       | integer | Always        | Per-symbol L3 sequence. Each logical mutation advances it by exactly one.                 |
| `trade_id`       | integer | Fill actions  | Trade that caused a `partial_fill` or `full_fill`.                                        |
| `timestamp`      | integer | Always        | Engine mutation or trade time in Unix epoch milliseconds.                                 |

`order_id` and `taker_order_id` are opaque, case-sensitive strings. They do not expose internal, account, or client order IDs. The same taking order uses the same public ID across its fills and, if an unfilled remainder later rests, its `open.order_id`.

#### Actions

| Action         | Required action-specific fields                                                                     | Local book effect                                                  |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `open`         | `order_id`, `side`, `price`, positive `delta_size`, equal positive `remaining_size`                 | Insert the new order at the back of the FIFO queue at its price.   |
| `modify`       | `order_id`, `side`, `price`, negative `delta_size`, positive `remaining_size`                       | Reduce the existing order in place without changing FIFO priority. |
| `cancel`       | `order_id`, `side`, `price`, negative `delta_size`, `remaining_size: "0"`                           | Remove the order without recording a trade.                        |
| `partial_fill` | Order fields plus `trade_id` and `taker_order_id`; negative `delta_size`; positive `remaining_size` | Reduce the maker order in place and retain its FIFO priority.      |
| `full_fill`    | Order fields plus `trade_id` and `taker_order_id`; negative `delta_size`; `remaining_size: "0"`     | Remove the fully filled maker order.                               |
| `clear`        | No order-specific fields                                                                            | Invalidate the local book and obtain a new snapshot.               |

`modify` is reserved for a real priority-preserving in-place reduction and is not currently emitted by a public order-entry operation. Strike's replace-order flow is represented by `cancel` followed by a new `open` with a different public order ID; it is never synthesized as `modify`.

#### Action examples

Open:

```json
{
  "type": "l3_update",
  "symbol": "BTC-USD",
  "action": "open",
  "order_id": "YL8wLzJfqGW_uIZ7qvzu5A",
  "side": "buy",
  "price": "117500.00",
  "delta_size": "0.15",
  "remaining_size": "0.15",
  "sequence": 918273,
  "timestamp": 1785480000001
}
```

Cancel:

```json
{
  "type": "l3_update",
  "symbol": "BTC-USD",
  "action": "cancel",
  "order_id": "YL8wLzJfqGW_uIZ7qvzu5A",
  "side": "buy",
  "price": "117500.00",
  "delta_size": "-0.11",
  "remaining_size": "0",
  "sequence": 918276,
  "timestamp": 1785480000201
}
```

Full fill:

```json
{
  "type": "l3_update",
  "symbol": "BTC-USD",
  "action": "full_fill",
  "order_id": "B0PmzcS4Zo9Dft7jLFzl8Q",
  "taker_order_id": "8CfeN3BBBOJLhNIx5ekcVw",
  "side": "sell",
  "price": "117510.00",
  "delta_size": "-0.50",
  "remaining_size": "0",
  "sequence": 918277,
  "trade_id": 771830,
  "timestamp": 1785480000305
}
```

Clear:

```json
{
  "type": "l3_update",
  "symbol": "BTC-USD",
  "action": "clear",
  "sequence": 918278,
  "timestamp": 1785480000400
}
```

### Snapshot

Fetch a complete book from:

```
GET /v2/l3/snapshot?symbol=BTC-USD
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "type": "l3_snapshot",
  "symbol": "BTC-USD",
  "last_sequence": 918274,
  "timestamp": 1785480000200,
  "bids": [
    {
      "price": "117500.00",
      "orders": [
        { "order_id": "YL8wLzJfqGW_uIZ7qvzu5A", "size": "0.11" },
        { "order_id": "8CfeN3BBBOJLhNIx5ekcVw", "size": "2.00" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "asks": [
    {
      "price": "117510.00",
      "orders": [
        { "order_id": "B0PmzcS4Zo9Dft7jLFzl8Q", "size": "0.50" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Snapshot rules:

* Bids are sorted by descending numeric price; asks by ascending numeric price.
* Orders at one price are in actual FIFO priority.
* `size` is the order's remaining visible size.
* `last_sequence` uses the same per-symbol sequence domain as WebSocket updates.
* The response includes every visible order and is never paginated or semantically truncated.
* Empty sides are returned as empty arrays.

The formal HTTP schema is in `strike-v2-l3-orders.openapi.yaml`.

### Bootstrap and recovery

A snapshot and the WebSocket stream must be combined in this order:

1. Open `/ws/l3`.
2. Send `SUBSCRIBE` and immediately buffer every `l3_update` for the symbol, including any update received before the acknowledgement.
3. After the subscription acknowledgement, request `/v2/l3/snapshot?symbol=BTC-USD`.
4. Replace the local book with the snapshot and set the local sequence to `last_sequence`.
5. Discard buffered updates with `sequence <= last_sequence`.
6. Apply the remaining buffered updates in sequence order. The first must be `last_sequence + 1`, and every update after it must be exactly one greater than the previous update.
7. Continue applying live updates using the same continuity check.

Sequence numbers are independent per symbol. If one connection subscribes to multiple symbols, maintain a separate book, buffer, and last sequence for each symbol.

Immediately stop applying updates and rebuild from a new snapshot when any of these occurs:

* an update sequence is not the previous sequence plus one;
* a `clear` action is received;
* the WebSocket closes or reconnects;
* the client cannot keep up with the stream;
* an update cannot be parsed or applied consistently to the local book.

There is no public replay endpoint. Never guess through a gap or continue using a stale local book.

### Error handling

Command errors have this shape:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": 400,
    "msg": "unsupported L3 channel"
  },
  "id": 1
}
```

Common command errors:

| Message                                       | Cause                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `invalid JSON`                                | The frame is not one valid JSON object.                         |
| `unsupported method`                          | The method is not `SUBSCRIBE` or `UNSUBSCRIBE`.                 |
| `params must contain at least one L3 channel` | `params` is missing, is not an array of strings, or is empty.   |
| `unsupported L3 channel`                      | The symbol is not enabled or the channel is not `{symbol}@l3`.  |
| `L3 subscription limit exceeded`              | The command would exceed 10 active channels on this connection. |

`unsupported L3 channel` and `L3 subscription limit exceeded` echo the command ID. Invalid JSON, invalid `params`, and unsupported methods use `id: null`.

The initial WebSocket HTTP upgrade can also fail with `400`, `403`, `429`, or `503`. In particular, `429` means a public request or connection limit was exceeded, and `503` means L3 state or distributed limiting is unavailable.

The server may close an established connection with:

| Close code | Meaning                                                                                   | Client action                                                            |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `1012`     | Service restart, publisher/readiness loss, Redis stream outage, or detected sequence gap. | Reconnect with backoff and bootstrap from a new snapshot.                |
| `1013`     | Slow consumer or distributed connection lease loss.                                       | Reduce processing pressure, reconnect with backoff, and bootstrap again. |
| `1001`     | Service shutdown.                                                                         | Reconnect with backoff and bootstrap again.                              |

Treat every disconnect as a recovery boundary even if the close reason is not available.

### Reference Implementation

{% tab title="Python" %}
Install the WebSocket dependency with `pip install websockets`.

```python
import asyncio
import contextlib
import json
import urllib.request
from typing import Any

import websockets

WS_URL = "wss://api-v2-testnet.strikefinance.org/ws/l3"
SNAPSHOT_URL = (
    "https://api-v2-testnet.strikefinance.org"
    "/v2/l3/snapshot?symbol=BTC-USD"
)
CHANNEL = "btc-usd@l3"


class RecoveryRequired(Exception):
    pass


def fetch_snapshot() -> dict[str, Any]:
    with urllib.request.urlopen(SNAPSHOT_URL, timeout=10) as response:
        return json.load(response)


def apply_snapshot(snapshot: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    # Replace your complete local book with snapshot["bids"] and snapshot["asks"].
    print("snapshot", snapshot["symbol"], snapshot["last_sequence"])


def apply_update(update: dict[str, Any], last_sequence: int) -> int:
    sequence = int(update["sequence"])
    if update["action"] == "clear" or sequence != last_sequence + 1:
        raise RecoveryRequired(
            f"clear or sequence gap: previous={last_sequence}, received={sequence}"
        )
    # Apply open/modify/cancel/partial_fill/full_fill to your local book here.
    print("update", update["action"], sequence)
    return sequence


def raise_command_error(message: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    if "error" in message:
        raise RecoveryRequired(message["error"].get("msg", "WebSocket error"))


async def read_messages(websocket, inbox: asyncio.Queue) -> None:
    try:
        async for raw in websocket:
            await inbox.put(json.loads(raw))
    except Exception as exc:
        await inbox.put(exc)


def unwrap(item: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if isinstance(item, Exception):
        raise RecoveryRequired(f"WebSocket closed: {item}")
    return item


async def run_once() -> None:
    async with websockets.connect(WS_URL, open_timeout=10, close_timeout=5) as ws:
        inbox: asyncio.Queue = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=4096)
        reader = asyncio.create_task(read_messages(ws, inbox))
        try:
            await ws.send(json.dumps({
                "method": "SUBSCRIBE",
                "params": [CHANNEL],
                "id": 1,
            }))

            pending: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
            while True:
                message = unwrap(await inbox.get())
                raise_command_error(message)
                if message.get("type") == "l3_update":
                    pending.append(message)
                elif message.get("id") == 1 and "result" in message:
                    break

            # The reader task keeps buffering WebSocket updates during this request.
            snapshot = await asyncio.to_thread(fetch_snapshot)
            while not inbox.empty():
                message = unwrap(inbox.get_nowait())
                raise_command_error(message)
                if message.get("type") == "l3_update":
                    pending.append(message)

            apply_snapshot(snapshot)
            last_sequence = int(snapshot["last_sequence"])
            for update in sorted(pending, key=lambda item: int(item["sequence"])):
                if int(update["sequence"]) <= last_sequence:
                    continue
                last_sequence = apply_update(update, last_sequence)

            while True:
                message = unwrap(await inbox.get())
                raise_command_error(message)
                if message.get("type") == "l3_update":
                    last_sequence = apply_update(message, last_sequence)
        finally:
            reader.cancel()
            with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                await reader


async def main() -> None:
    delay = 1
    while True:
        try:
            await run_once()
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"L3 recovery required: {exc}; retrying in {delay}s")
            await asyncio.sleep(delay)
            delay = min(delay * 2, 30)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

{% tab title="TypeScript" %}
Install the dependencies with `npm install ws` and `npm install --save-dev tsx @types/ws`, then run the file with `npx tsx l3.ts`.

```typescript
import WebSocket from "ws";

const WS_URL = "wss://api-v2-testnet.strikefinance.org/ws/l3";
const SNAPSHOT_URL =
  "https://api-v2-testnet.strikefinance.org/v2/l3/snapshot?symbol=BTC-USD";
const CHANNEL = "btc-usd@l3";

type L3Update = {
  type: "l3_update";
  symbol: string;
  action: "open" | "modify" | "cancel" | "partial_fill" | "full_fill" | "clear";
  sequence: number;
  timestamp: number;
  order_id?: string;
  taker_order_id?: string;
  side?: "buy" | "sell";
  price?: string;
  delta_size?: string;
  remaining_size?: string;
  trade_id?: number;
};

type L3Snapshot = {
  type: "l3_snapshot";
  symbol: string;
  last_sequence: number;
  timestamp: number;
  bids: Array<{ price: string; orders: Array<{ order_id: string; size: string }> }>;
  asks: Array<{ price: string; orders: Array<{ order_id: string; size: string }> }>;
};

type Message = L3Update & {
  id?: string | number;
  result?: null;
  error?: { code: number; msg: string };
};

class Inbox {
  private messages: Message[] = [];
  private wake?: () => void;
  private failure?: Error;

  push(message: Message): void {
    this.messages.push(message);
    this.wake?.();
  }

  fail(error: Error): void {
    this.failure ??= error;
    this.wake?.();
  }

  async next(): Promise<Message> {
    while (this.messages.length === 0) {
      if (this.failure) throw this.failure;
      await new Promise<void>((resolve) => { this.wake = resolve; });
      this.wake = undefined;
    }
    return this.messages.shift()!;
  }

  drain(): Message[] {
    if (this.failure) throw this.failure;
    const messages = this.messages;
    this.messages = [];
    return messages;
  }
}

const applySnapshot = (snapshot: L3Snapshot): void => {
  // Replace your complete local book with snapshot.bids and snapshot.asks.
  console.log("snapshot", snapshot.symbol, snapshot.last_sequence);
};

const applyUpdate = (update: L3Update, lastSequence: number): number => {
  if (update.action === "clear" || update.sequence !== lastSequence + 1) {
    throw new Error(
      `clear or sequence gap: previous=${lastSequence}, received=${update.sequence}`,
    );
  }
  // Apply open/modify/cancel/partial_fill/full_fill to your local book here.
  console.log("update", update.action, update.sequence);
  return update.sequence;
};

const checkCommandError = (message: Message): void => {
  if (message.error) throw new Error(message.error.msg);
};

async function runOnce(): Promise<void> {
  const ws = new WebSocket(WS_URL);
  const inbox = new Inbox();

  ws.on("message", (data) => {
    try {
      inbox.push(JSON.parse(data.toString()) as Message);
    } catch {
      inbox.fail(new Error("invalid JSON from server"));
    }
  });
  ws.on("close", () => inbox.fail(new Error("WebSocket closed")));
  ws.on("error", (error) => inbox.fail(error));

  try {
    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
      ws.once("open", resolve);
      ws.once("error", reject);
    });
    ws.send(JSON.stringify({ method: "SUBSCRIBE", params: [CHANNEL], id: 1 }));

    const pending: L3Update[] = [];
    while (true) {
      const message = await inbox.next();
      checkCommandError(message);
      if (message.type === "l3_update") pending.push(message);
      else if (message.id === 1 && Object.hasOwn(message, "result")) break;
    }

    // WebSocket events continue accumulating in Inbox during this request.
    const response = await fetch(SNAPSHOT_URL, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) });
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`snapshot failed: HTTP ${response.status}`);
    const snapshot = await response.json() as L3Snapshot;

    for (const message of inbox.drain()) {
      checkCommandError(message);
      if (message.type === "l3_update") pending.push(message);
    }

    applySnapshot(snapshot);
    let lastSequence = snapshot.last_sequence;
    pending.sort((a, b) => a.sequence - b.sequence);
    for (const update of pending) {
      if (update.sequence <= lastSequence) continue;
      lastSequence = applyUpdate(update, lastSequence);
    }

    while (true) {
      const message = await inbox.next();
      checkCommandError(message);
      if (message.type === "l3_update") {
        lastSequence = applyUpdate(message, lastSequence);
      }
    }
  } finally {
    ws.close();
  }
}

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  let delay = 1_000;
  while (true) {
    try {
      await runOnce();
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(`L3 recovery required: ${String(error)}; retrying in ${delay}ms`);
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delay));
      delay = Math.min(delay * 2, 30_000);
    }
  }
}

main().catch(console.error);
```

Install the WebSocket dependency with `go get github.com/gorilla/websocket`.

```go
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"sort"
	"time"

	"github.com/gorilla/websocket"
)

const (
	wsURL       = "wss://api-v2-testnet.strikefinance.org/ws/l3"
	snapshotURL = "https://api-v2-testnet.strikefinance.org/v2/l3/snapshot?symbol=BTC-USD"
	channel     = "btc-usd@l3"
)

type commandError struct {
	Code int    `json:"code"`
	Msg  string `json:"msg"`
}

type message struct {
	Type          string          `json:"type"`
	Symbol        string          `json:"symbol"`
	Action        string          `json:"action"`
	OrderID       string          `json:"order_id"`
	TakerOrderID  string          `json:"taker_order_id"`
	Side          string          `json:"side"`
	Price         string          `json:"price"`
	DeltaSize     string          `json:"delta_size"`
	RemainingSize string          `json:"remaining_size"`
	Sequence      uint64          `json:"sequence"`
	TradeID       uint64          `json:"trade_id"`
	Timestamp     int64           `json:"timestamp"`
	ID            json.RawMessage `json:"id"`
	Result        json.RawMessage `json:"result"`
	Error         *commandError   `json:"error"`
}

type snapshot struct {
	Type         string `json:"type"`
	Symbol       string `json:"symbol"`
	LastSequence uint64 `json:"last_sequence"`
	Bids         []any  `json:"bids"`
	Asks         []any  `json:"asks"`
}

type readResult struct {
	message message
	err     error
}

func readMessages(conn *websocket.Conn, output chan<- readResult) {
	defer close(output)
	for {
		_, data, err := conn.ReadMessage()
		if err != nil {
			output <- readResult{err: err}
			return
		}
		var value message
		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &value); err != nil {
			output <- readResult{err: fmt.Errorf("invalid JSON from server: %w", err)}
			return
		}
		output <- readResult{message: value}
	}
}

func next(input <-chan readResult) (message, error) {
	result, ok := <-input
	if !ok {
		return message{}, fmt.Errorf("WebSocket closed")
	}
	if result.err != nil {
		return message{}, result.err
	}
	if result.message.Error != nil {
		return message{}, fmt.Errorf("WebSocket error: %s", result.message.Error.Msg)
	}
	return result.message, nil
}

func fetchSnapshot() (snapshot, error) {
	client := &http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second}
	response, err := client.Get(snapshotURL)
	if err != nil {
		return snapshot{}, err
	}
	defer response.Body.Close()
	if response.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		return snapshot{}, fmt.Errorf("snapshot failed: HTTP %d", response.StatusCode)
	}
	var value snapshot
	err = json.NewDecoder(response.Body).Decode(&value)
	return value, err
}

func applySnapshot(value snapshot) {
	// Replace your complete local book with value.Bids and value.Asks.
	fmt.Println("snapshot", value.Symbol, value.LastSequence)
}

func applyUpdate(value message, lastSequence uint64) (uint64, error) {
	if value.Action == "clear" || value.Sequence != lastSequence+1 {
		return lastSequence, fmt.Errorf(
			"clear or sequence gap: previous=%d, received=%d",
			lastSequence, value.Sequence,
		)
	}
	// Apply open/modify/cancel/partial_fill/full_fill to your local book here.
	fmt.Println("update", value.Action, value.Sequence)
	return value.Sequence, nil
}

func runOnce() error {
	conn, _, err := websocket.DefaultDialer.Dial(wsURL, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer conn.Close()

	inbox := make(chan readResult, 4096)
	go readMessages(conn, inbox)
	if err := conn.WriteJSON(map[string]any{
		"method": "SUBSCRIBE", "params": []string{channel}, "id": 1,
	}); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	pending := make([]message, 0)
	for {
		value, err := next(inbox)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if value.Type == "l3_update" {
			pending = append(pending, value)
		} else if string(value.ID) == "1" && len(value.Result) > 0 {
			break
		}
	}

	// The reader goroutine keeps buffering WebSocket updates during this request.
	book, err := fetchSnapshot()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

drain:
	for {
		select {
		case result, ok := <-inbox:
			if !ok {
				return fmt.Errorf("WebSocket closed")
			}
			if result.err != nil {
				return result.err
			}
			if result.message.Error != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("WebSocket error: %s", result.message.Error.Msg)
			}
			if result.message.Type == "l3_update" {
				pending = append(pending, result.message)
			}
		default:
			break drain
		}
	}

	applySnapshot(book)
	lastSequence := book.LastSequence
	sort.Slice(pending, func(i, j int) bool {
		return pending[i].Sequence < pending[j].Sequence
	})
	for _, update := range pending {
		if update.Sequence <= lastSequence {
			continue
		}
		lastSequence, err = applyUpdate(update, lastSequence)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}

	for {
		value, err := next(inbox)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if value.Type == "l3_update" {
			lastSequence, err = applyUpdate(value, lastSequence)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
	}
}

func main() {
	delay := time.Second
	for {
		if err := runOnce(); err != nil {
			log.Printf("L3 recovery required: %v; retrying in %s", err, delay)
			time.Sleep(delay)
			if delay < 30*time.Second {
				delay *= 2
			}
		}
	}
}
```

Add `anyhow`, `futures-util`, `reqwest` with `json` and `rustls-tls`, `serde` with `derive`, `serde_json`, `tokio` with `full`, and `tokio-tungstenite` with `rustls-tls-webpki-roots` to `Cargo.toml`.

```rust
use anyhow::{anyhow, bail, Result};
use futures_util::{SinkExt, StreamExt};
use serde::Deserialize;
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use std::cmp::min;
use tokio::sync::mpsc;
use tokio::time::{sleep, Duration};
use tokio_tungstenite::{connect_async, tungstenite::Message};

const WS_URL: &str = "wss://api-v2-testnet.strikefinance.org/ws/l3";
const SNAPSHOT_URL: &str =
    "https://api-v2-testnet.strikefinance.org/v2/l3/snapshot?symbol=BTC-USD";
const CHANNEL: &str = "btc-usd@l3";

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
struct Update {
    action: String,
    sequence: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct Snapshot {
    symbol: String,
    last_sequence: u64,
    bids: Vec<Value>,
    asks: Vec<Value>,
}

fn command_error(value: &Value) -> Option<String> {
    value
        .get("error")
        .and_then(|error| error.get("msg"))
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .map(str::to_owned)
}

fn update_from(value: &Value) -> Result<Option<Update>> {
    if value.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) == Some("l3_update") {
        return Ok(Some(serde_json::from_value(value.clone())?));
    }
    Ok(None)
}

fn apply_snapshot(snapshot: &Snapshot) {
    // Replace your complete local book with snapshot.bids and snapshot.asks.
    println!(
        "snapshot {} {} ({} bid levels, {} ask levels)",
        snapshot.symbol,
        snapshot.last_sequence,
        snapshot.bids.len(),
        snapshot.asks.len()
    );
}

fn apply_update(update: &Update, last_sequence: u64) -> Result<u64> {
    if update.action == "clear" || update.sequence != last_sequence + 1 {
        bail!(
            "clear or sequence gap: previous={}, received={}",
            last_sequence,
            update.sequence
        );
    }
    // Apply open/modify/cancel/partial_fill/full_fill to your local book here.
    println!("update {} {}", update.action, update.sequence);
    Ok(update.sequence)
}

fn collect(value: Value, pending: &mut Vec<Update>) -> Result<()> {
    if let Some(message) = command_error(&value) {
        bail!("WebSocket error: {message}");
    }
    if let Some(update) = update_from(&value)? {
        pending.push(update);
    }
    Ok(())
}

async fn receive(inbox: &mut mpsc::Receiver<Result<Value, String>>) -> Result<Value> {
    match inbox.recv().await {
        Some(Ok(value)) => Ok(value),
        Some(Err(error)) => Err(anyhow!(error)),
        None => bail!("WebSocket closed"),
    }
}

async fn run_once() -> Result<()> {
    let (websocket, _) = connect_async(WS_URL).await?;
    let (mut writer, mut reader) = websocket.split();
    writer
        .send(Message::Text(
            json!({"method": "SUBSCRIBE", "params": [CHANNEL], "id": 1})
                .to_string()
                .into(),
        ))
        .await?;

    let (sender, mut inbox) = mpsc::channel::<Result<Value, String>>(4096);
    let reader_task = tokio::spawn(async move {
        while let Some(frame) = reader.next().await {
            let value = match frame {
                Ok(Message::Text(text)) => serde_json::from_str(&text)
                    .map_err(|error| format!("invalid JSON from server: {error}")),
                Ok(Message::Close(_)) => Err("WebSocket closed".to_owned()),
                Ok(_) => continue,
                Err(error) => Err(format!("WebSocket read failed: {error}")),
            };
            let failed = value.is_err();
            if sender.send(value).await.is_err() || failed {
                break;
            }
        }
    });

    let result = async {
        let mut pending = Vec::new();
        loop {
            let value = receive(&mut inbox).await?;
            if let Some(message) = command_error(&value) {
                bail!("WebSocket error: {message}");
            }
            if let Some(update) = update_from(&value)? {
                pending.push(update);
            } else if value.get("id") == Some(&json!(1)) && value.get("result").is_some() {
                break;
            }
        }

        // The reader task keeps buffering WebSocket updates during this request.
        let snapshot = reqwest::Client::new()
            .get(SNAPSHOT_URL)
            .timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))
            .send()
            .await?
            .error_for_status()?
            .json::<Snapshot>()
            .await?;

        while let Ok(item) = inbox.try_recv() {
            collect(item.map_err(|error| anyhow!(error))?, &mut pending)?;
        }

        apply_snapshot(&snapshot);
        let mut last_sequence = snapshot.last_sequence;
        pending.sort_by_key(|update| update.sequence);
        for update in pending {
            if update.sequence <= last_sequence {
                continue;
            }
            last_sequence = apply_update(&update, last_sequence)?;
        }

        loop {
            let value = receive(&mut inbox).await?;
            if let Some(message) = command_error(&value) {
                bail!("WebSocket error: {message}");
            }
            if let Some(update) = update_from(&value)? {
                last_sequence = apply_update(&update, last_sequence)?;
            }
        }
    }
    .await;

    reader_task.abort();
    drop(writer);
    result
}

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    let mut delay_seconds = 1;
    loop {
        if let Err(error) = run_once().await {
            eprintln!(
                "L3 recovery required: {error}; retrying in {delay_seconds}s"
            );
            sleep(Duration::from_secs(delay_seconds)).await;
            delay_seconds = min(delay_seconds * 2, 30);
        }
    }
}
```

# Tokenomics

**STRIKE Utility**

The Strike Token (STRIKE) offers a range of utilities within the Strike Finance ecosystem, making it a vital component for users. The key utilities of STRIKE include:

1. Staking: STRIKE holders can stake their tokens and earn a percentage of protocol fees.
2. Governance: STRIKE holders can participate in the protocol’s governance, voting on important decisions such as upgrades, new feature implementations, and changes to fee structures.
3. Trading Fees: Holders of STRIKE will have discounted trading fees for using the platform. The discounted fee for STRIKE holders can be stacked on top of the discounted fee when using STRIKE as additional collateral.

### ​**Distribution** <a href="#distribution" id="distribution"></a>

**STRIKE** is the platform token for the **Strike Finance** protocol. There are a total of 25 million (25,000,000) **STRIKE** tokens. The allocation for **STRIKE** is detailed below from largest to smallest:

* **Public Sale:** 60% (15,000,000 tokens)
* **Team and Advisors**: 15% (3,750,000 tokens)
* **Liquidity:** 12% (3,000,000 tokens)
* **DAO**: 13% (3,250,000 tokens)

The total public allocation is 85%, with 15% for team and advisors.

The distribution is as follows:

**Tokenomics Chart**

### ​**Emissions** <a href="#emissions" id="emissions"></a>

Emissions will be simple and concise. There will be 72% of tokens initially in circulation (public + liquidity). The additional 15% from team allocation will be fully unlocked after 30 months (full details below) for a circulating supply of 87%, and the final 13% (DAO treasury) will be decided by community members at a later time.

### ​**Vesting** <a href="#vesting" id="vesting"></a>

DAO vesting will be entirely up to the voting of STRIKE holders. This can be used for anything the community sees fit such as incentives, initiatives, funding future development, etc.

Team vesting is simple. Starting from the token generation event, there is a 6 month period where there are no unlocked tokens. After that, tokens will unlock linearly monthly over the span of 24 months (2 years).


# Staking

## V2 Liquid Staking Rewards

<figure><img src="https://3104501468-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2Fl6nT3DjbRRXrBD1ATav2%2Fuploads%2FXtvLABiQwg1D0FCMBLtA%2FScreenshot%202026-05-05%20at%204.51.33%E2%80%AFAM.png?alt=media&amp;token=4c356237-463a-4172-a172-02f6cb862dbf" alt=""><figcaption></figcaption></figure>

Strike V2 liquid staking lets you earn a share of revenue generated by the Strike platform while keeping your $STRIKE usable across supported DeFi positions, or by simply holding it in your wallet.

### Start Here: Opt In First

To earn V2 liquid staking rewards, you must first opt in from the Strike staking UI.

Once you stake through the UI, Strike links reward tracking to that staking wallet. From that point forward, you do not need to manually register each DeFi position. Strike automatically detects eligible $STRIKE activity connected to that same wallet across supported platforms.

The key rule is simple: opt in once, then keep your eligible $STRIKE activity connected to the same staking wallet.

### How V2 Liquid Staking Works

Instead of requiring your $STRIKE to sit idle, V2 liquid staking uses daily balance snapshots and time-weighted average balance (TWAB) accounting.

This means you can stake through Strike, then continue using your $STRIKE in supported DEX liquidity positions or lending markets and still qualify for rewards.

There is no lockup. Staked $STRIKE and distributed rewards can be withdrawn at any time, subject to the normal wallet, DeFi protocol, and Strike withdrawal flows.

### V1 Migration

All future staking rewards will be distributed through the new Strike V2 platform. If you are currently staking on V1, please migrate your stake to V2 to continue earning rewards.

V1 staking is being deprecated and will no longer be used for future reward distributions. To read more about the migration [V1 - V2 Migration](/tokenomics/markdown/v1-v2-migration).

### Reward Funding

The main revenue source for Strike is the opening fee paid when traders open perpetual positions.

Opening fees are split between Strike and liquidity providers. This split may change over time. 100% of the opening fees that go to Strike are distributed to eligible stakers once every 15 days.

Rewards are deposited directly into your Strike account as USDM. Once deposited, rewards are released and can be withdrawn from Strike.

V1 platform rewards will also be converted to USDM, deposited into Strike during each distribution period, and fully released.

### Withdrawing rewards

Every distribution your account balance on the Strike platform will increase. You can use this balance to place trades, deposit into vaults, or withdraw to your wallet directly in the form of a stablecoin.&#x20;

### Eligibility

To earn rewards, your $STRIKE must be associated with the same wallet you used to opt in from the Strike staking UI.

After you opt in, eligible $STRIKE can qualify automatically from supported activity connected to that wallet, including:

| Eligible Activity                           | How It Counts                                  |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Buy $STRIKE and hold in your staking wallet | Automatically detected                         |
| Used in supported DEX liquidity positions   | Automatically detected from the staking wallet |
| Used in supported lending positions         | Automatically detected from the staking wallet |

To receive full period weight, keep your $STRIKE qualified for the full 3-epoch distribution period. If your $STRIKE is unstaked or moved away from the staking wallet before distribution, it stops qualifying for future snapshots and your reward weight is reduced by TWAB.

Do not stake with one wallet and then send the $STRIKE to another wallet. If the $STRIKE is moved to another wallet, it will not count toward rewards for the original staking wallet.

### Daily Snapshots

Daily snapshots are taken at 00:00:00 UTC. This fixed snapshot time is used so everyone can see exactly when balances are measured.

A snapshot records how much eligible $STRIKE a staking wallet has at that point in time. Across a reward period, those snapshots are used to calculate a time-weighted average.

| What Matters                       | How It Affects Rewards                         |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| How much eligible $STRIKE you have | More eligible $STRIKE earns more reward weight |
| How long you keep it eligible      | Longer participation earns more reward weight  |

Rewards are not based only on your balance at the final distribution moment. They are based on how much eligible $STRIKE you had throughout the reward period.

### Joining Late

You can still receive rewards if you enter a supported position before the distribution period ends. For example, if you join one day before a distribution, your eligible $STRIKE can still count for that final day.

However, because rewards are time-weighted, joining late earns much less than participating for the full period.

| Example                            | Reward Weight      |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| 1,000 $STRIKE eligible for 30 days | 30,000 STRIKE-days |
| 1,000 $STRIKE eligible for 1 day   | 1,000 STRIKE-days  |

In this example, the wallet that joined for only one day earns about 1/30th of the reward weight of the wallet that participated for the full 30 days, even though both wallets had the same amount of $STRIKE.

### Why It Is Fair

The snapshot system is designed so rewards go to users who actually keep $STRIKE eligible over time.

Because rewards are time-weighted:

| Behavior                                    | Outcome                                  |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Holding eligible $STRIKE for longer         | Earns proportionally more reward weight  |
| Adding $STRIKE shortly before distribution  | Counts only for the time it was eligible |
| Removing $STRIKE before the end of a period | Stops earning future reward weight       |
| Moving in only at the last minute           | Does not earn full-period rewards        |

This makes the system difficult to game. A user cannot move $STRIKE into a supported position right before distribution and receive the same rewards as someone who supported the system for the entire period.

### Truly Liquid Staking

V2 liquid staking is designed so you can keep your $STRIKE productive.

After opting in from the staking UI, you can use your $STRIKE in supported DeFi positions, including DEX LPs and lending platforms, while still earning Strike revenue rewards.

You do not need to take any extra staking action for each DeFi position. Strike automatically picks up supported $STRIKE activity from the same staking wallet.

### How To Stake

1. Go to `app.strikefinance.org/staking`.
2. Sign in with the wallet you want to use for staking.
3. Use single address mode.
4. Click Stake.
5. Keep your $STRIKE activity connected to that staking wallet.

After staking, you can continue using your $STRIKE in supported DeFi positions from the same wallet.

### Cooldown And Start Date

There will be a cooldown period during the V1 to V2 transition.

| Date         | Update                    |
| ------------ | ------------------------- |
| May 9, 2026  | Distribution skipped      |
| May 15, 2026 | V2 reward counting starts |

Users should migrate their stake to V2 immediately. No rewards will be lost during the migration period.

# V1 - V2 Migration

### V1 To V2 Staking Migration

Strike is moving staking rewards from the V1 staking flow into V2 liquid staking.

V2 liquid staking is designed to make $STRIKE more useful while still rewarding long-term stakers. After migrating, you can stake through Strike, use **single address mode**, and continue using your $STRIKE in supported DEX LPs or lending positions from the same staking wallet.

{% hint style="info" %}
Users should migrate their stake to V2 immediately. The May 9, 2026 distribution will be skipped during the cooldown period, and V2 staking reward counting starts on May 15, 2026.
{% endhint %}

#### Important Dates

| Date               | What Happens                                                                                |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **May 9, 2026**    | Distribution skipped during the cooldown period                                             |
| **May 15, 2026**   | V2 reward counting begins                                                                   |
| After May 15, 2026 | Daily snapshots at **00:00:00 UTC** count toward future distributions                       |
| June 1st, 2026     | First distribution with liquid staking, distributing accumulated V1 and V2 staking rewards. |

#### What Changes In V2

V1 staking rewards are moving into the Strike V2 account flow.

In V2:

* Rewards are calculated using daily snapshots and TWAB
* Snapshots happen every day at **00:00:00 UTC**
* Rewards are deposited into your Strike account as **USDM**
* Rewards are released during each distribution period
* Rewards can be withdrawn from Strike as USDM
* Your $STRIKE can still be used in supported DEX LPs and lending positions

V1 platform rewards will be converted to USDM, deposited into Strike during each distribution period, and fully released.

#### Migration Steps

1. Go to [app.strikefinance.org/staking](https://app.strikefinance.org/staking)
2. Sign in with the wallet you use for staking
3. Make sure you are using **single address mode**
4. Click **Stake**
5. Keep your qualifying $STRIKE activity connected to that same wallet

After staking, you can use your $STRIKE in supported DeFi positions such as DEX LPs or lending markets.

#### Single Address Mode

Use **single address mode** when migrating to V2.

Single address mode makes it easier for Strike to track your staking wallet and the $STRIKE positions connected to it. This is important because V2 rewards depend on daily snapshots of the staking wallet and its supported DeFi positions.

#### Wallet Rule

Your staking wallet is the wallet that must remain connected to your qualifying $STRIKE.

You can:

* Stake from your wallet
* Use $STRIKE from that wallet in supported DEX LPs
* Use $STRIKE from that wallet in supported lending positions

You should not:

* Stake with one wallet and send $STRIKE to another wallet
* Split qualifying $STRIKE across wallets that are not connected to your staking setup
* Expect another wallet's $STRIKE to count for your staking wallet

{% hint style="info" %}
V2 liquid staking is liquid, but it is wallet-based. The $STRIKE can move into supported DeFi positions, but it must remain associated with the staking wallet.
{% endhint %}

#### Why TWAB Matters

TWAB stands for time-weighted average balance.

TWAB prevents users from gaming the system by adding a large $STRIKE balance right before the distribution. Instead, rewards are based on how much qualifying $STRIKE was held over time across the full distribution period.

This makes rewards fairer for users who keep their $STRIKE staked or active in supported DeFi positions throughout the period.

#### Migration Checklist

* Sign in at [app.strikefinance.org/staking](https://app.strikefinance.org/staking)
* Use **single address mode**
* Click **Stake**
* Keep qualifying $STRIKE tied to the staking wallet
* Migrate before V2 reward counting starts on **May 15, 2026**
